title: Will The Agit Kabayel Era Begin on Saturday in Dusseldorf?
summary: What to Know WBC World Heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel and challenger Nelson Hysa are prepared for their championship fight on Saturday, November 28 in front of 50,000 fans at the Merkur Spiel Arena in Dusseldorf. Kabayel will make the first defense of his title against the lesser-known Albanian challenger, who would be his country’s first […]
content: What to Know WBC World Heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel and challenger Nelson Hysa are prepared for their championship fight on Saturday, November 28 in front of 50,000 fans at the Merkur Spiel Arena in Dusseldorf. Kabayel will make the first defense of his title against the lesser-known Albanian challenger, who would be his country’s first boxing world champion if he wins. The fight will air live in the U.S. on DAZN Boxing starting at 1 p.m. ET / 10 a.m. PT in the U.S. and 6 p.m. GMT in the UK. On Saturday, November 28, at the Rudolf Weber Arena in Dusseldorf near Agit Kabayel’s hometown, it will be 11 years to the day that Wladimir Klitschko lost to Tyson Fury in the same arena. German fans who embraced the Ukrainian Klitschko brothers as their own haven’t had much to cheer since they retired. Now, their hopes have been raised by Germany’s newest champion, WBC World Heavyweight champion Agit Kabayel. Agit Kabayel says Nelson Hysa is a great trash talk, and not much else. Photo: Queensberry Promotions Kabayel would like to change his status as the boxing world’s forgotten heavyweight champion. The native of Bochum is already a star at home. His appearance against Damian Knyba in January sold out the 13.000-seat Rudolf Weber Arena in Oberhausen before an enthusiastic audience. Because of that enthusiastic response, Queensberry Promotions decided to stage Saturday’s fight in a 54,600-capacity arena. Only a handful of fighters can fill that many seats: Canelo Álvarez , Jake Paul, Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua, Katie Taylor. And now, Agit Kabayel, with 50,000 tickets sold. According to Kabayel’s opponent, Nelson Hysa of Albania, thousands of those tickets were sold to his devoted Albanian fans. The fight also takes place on Albanian Independence Day. Kabayel’s Quiet Path to the Heavyweight Title Agit Kabayel got the boxing world’s attention with his win over Zhilei Zhang to win the Interim WBC World Heavyweight title in February 2025. Photo: Mark Robinson, Matchroom Boxing Kabayel (26-0, 18 KOs), age 34, became the WBC Interim Heavyweight champion with a win over Zhilei Zhang of China in 2025. He was upgraded to full champion status after unified champion Oleksandr Usyk of Ukraine relinquished his WBC belt in June . Kabayel captured the boxing world’s attention with wins over Arslanbek Makhmudov and Frank Sanchez. Knowledgeable fans have gravitated to Kabayel, who is Kurdish by heritage. He speaks English, German, and Kurdish fluently. Kabayel had hoped to face Usyk. He joined Usyk in the ring after his knockout win over Rico Verhoeven in Egypt. But it didn’t materialize. With the top ten heavyweights already booked ( Fury vs Joshua , Dubois vs Parker , and a potential Benavidez vs Usyk matchup, Hysa (25-0, 23 KOs) Hysa accepted the matchup with Kabayel. Hysa enjoyed a long amateur career and didn’t turn pro until age 37 in 2022, and his resume has no recognizable names. Now at age 42, he is determined to become the first-ever world champion from Albania in any division. “I want only the big fights, but none of the big guys are available,” said Kabayel. “Now I will teach (Hysa) respect. Nelson is my focus now. But after this fight, it’s a unification fight. This is my dream. I want all the belts.” Kabayel called Hysa a better trash talker, but on November 28 they would find out who is the better boxer. Agit Kabayel Proud to Represent German and Kurdish Heritage Agit Kabayel said he’s proud to represent both his German and Kurdish heritage. Photo: Queensberry Promotions “I’m proud to box under the German flag with my Kurdish roots and really happy to do that … It’s all about the unity, and it doesn’t matter what kind of religion. It’s just about the sports, and people know my country, Germany, and know the country where I derive from,” said Kabayel in German at the final pre-fight news conference in Dusseldorf on Thursday. “It will be an unbelievable feeling when I step into the ring, representing both countries. Germany gave me so much. I’m going to give it back. But I have my Kurdish roots, and I am proud to bring that to the world,” said Kabayel. Asked about his plan for the fight, Kabayel was cagey. “I’m well prepared. I’m giving nothing away about my game plan, and my coach is really happy that we don’t do training anymore. My hands are in the ice bucket, so everything is prepared.” Nelson Hysa: “I Love You, Albania!” Nelson Hysa would become Albania’s first world champion in boxing history with a win on Saturday. Photo: Queensberry Promotions Hysa acknowledged Saturday is a big fight both for him and for his country. “He’s a good boxer. He has done very good in boxing, and I’m proud that you support him,” said Hysa to the German fans. “I want to thank my people supporting me from all over the world … Albanians coming to support me. Thank you. I love you, Albania!” Hysa hinted that Kabayel has fragile hands. “I am happy for the coach of Agit that he will not have more problem with hands. But I think Agit will have problem with hands Saturday. “You need to believe, because everything is possible in life and in boxing. I will answer you: Yes, I come to win. I prepare to win, and I will win.” “We are fully prepared, and we hope we will do a good fight. And like you know, I’m every time realistic. So after we will win the match, the other match, the rematch will be in Albania. I will invite all of you to come in Albania to see how beautiful Albania is,” said Hysa. Without a doubt, Kabayel is a clear favorite among oddsmakers. But he said he knows what it’s like to be the person whose chance for success is in doubt. “I was the underdog, an underdog over and over again. Right now I’m the favorite, and there is no pressure. But I’m going to be better and improve from fight to fight. I’m Agit Kabayel. I want to be better in every fight, and I want to be improve, improve that. I want to show that to the people, and there’s no pressure for me. I’m the favorite right now. That’s it. The Kabayel Era: Inspired by Tyson Fury Kabayel declared Saturday will be the beginning of a new era: the Kabayel Era. It’s certainly going to be an era. It’s the new era of Agit Kabayel. I’m going to be the new champion. I’m writing my own chapter. I’m writing new history, and the fight 11 years ago when Wladimir Klitschko lost to Tyson Fury, it was bad for Germany. “But Tyson Fury kind of inspired me, and now I got the same manager, and this was kind of the starting point, and he inspired me to keep on fighting and to bring it all on the line. It’s all about boxing. We are going to let the fists speak in the ring. It’s not about Albanian people, and it’s not about Kurdish people. It’s all about the two guys in the ring,” said Kabayel. Prediction: Albania Must Wait A Little Longer Observers claim Hysa had an outstanding training camp, running through sparring partners and doing damage. But he lacks mobility and hasn’t demonstrated the punch volume that can fend off Kabayel. Kabayel’s high-volume pressure style is built around relentless body punching and heavy combinations. His sustained bodywork to the ribs and liver wears his opponents down over rounds, rather than relying solely on a single lights-out shot to the head. Expect Kabayel to get right to work against Hysa, breaking him down and draining his spirit. He’s riding a six-fight knockout streak since 2022 and hasn’t gone more than seven rounds. He won’t make it that far against Hysa. We predict a TKO win for Kabayel in rounds five or six. Kabayel vs Hysa Undercard Lineup Four bouts have been set for the undercard at Merkur Spiel-Arena in Dusseldorf, Germany. A cruiserweight matchup features London native Aloys Youmbi (12-1, 9 KOs) facing Germany-based Artur Mann (23-6, 14 KOs) of Kazakhstan. Serbia’s Gleb Bakshi (7-0, 5 KOs) and Germany’s Serhat Parlak (8-1, 3 KOs) square off at middleweight. Germany’s Granit Shala (18-2, 7 KOs) and Iceland’s Kolbeinn Kristinsson (20-0, 14 KOs) clash at heavyweight. Simon Zachenhuber of Erding, Germany (29-2, 18 KOs) vs. Alexander Rigas of Munich (22-3, 10 KOs) in an all-Bayern super middleweight scrap.

title: Ex-Colorado State AD, former players raise alarm over Jim Mora and staff conduct
summary: Former Colorado State players have sent a letter to the university's governing board to address concerns about Jim Mora and his coaching staff.
content: Things appear to continue to get messier for Jim Mora at Colorado State. According to The Coloradan — part of the USA TODAY Network — nearly two dozen former Colorado State players are asking the university’s governing board to address concerns in what they describe as "inappropriate behaviors" from Mora and his staff and "the lack of response by athletic department leadership." Mora is in his first season at Colorado State after being hired from UConn last offseason. Week 13 bold predictions: Rivalry weekend could wreck some playoff dreams The Colorado State players who wrote and sent the letter to the Colorado State University System Board of Governors on Nov. 25 include former Rams quarterback and athletic director Jack Graham, former defensive back Erik Olson and former linebacker Nate Kvamme. The letter does not specifically ask the Colorado State University System Board of Governors to fire Mora or Colorado State athletic director John Weber, but brings forth their worry about the "welfare of the student athletes" in the program. "As former CSU football players, we want to convey a sense of urgency and resolve to support the University in rebuilding the integrity, culture and reputation of the Athletic Department and our football program," the letter reads. "Our experiences at CSU delivered great lessons and guidance for our adult lives. "We learned to compete and win. We had support to study and succeed in our academic careers. We were given the opportunity to be part of teams that represented commitment, hard work, integrity, respect and pride. We left CSU as better people." Graham additionally brought up several "red flag" incidents that he believes are egregious enough for Colorado State to fire Mora "for cause" under the terms of the five-year contract they signed him to last December. These "red flags" include: the program’s entire equipment room staff reportedly quitting at the beginning of the season or late spring due to "abusive behavior toward them by Jim Mora," damage allegedly done to the visitors’ locker room following a loss at Texas State on Oct. 25, not believing Mora's side of the story on the firing of former Rams defensive coordinator Tyson Summers in the middle of a game against Oregon State on Oct. 3 and a physical altercation between strength and conditioning coach Shelton Bynum and offensive lineman Toriyan Johnson amongst others. REQYIRED READING: Pac-12 flex week is set: Who will Boise State, others play? "Is the University providing the culture, leadership, support and resources these athletes need to be good human beings, strong competitors and lifelong proud alumnae of CSU?," the letter reads. "... We believe not; rather, they are seeing the antithesis of these critical values." Under Mora this season, the Rams have the No.4 scoring offense in the Pac-12 at 33.7 points per game, but one of the worst defenses in the conference and country. The Rams rank dead last in the Pac-12 in both scoring defense at 47.7 points per game and total defense at 548.1 total yards allowed per game. The Rams have won just once in their last nine games and have lost each of their last four games. In their four-game losing skid, Colorado State has been outscored by opponents 217-101. Colorado State ends its regular season at 6 p.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 28 against No. 21 Boise State . title: Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Iowa
summary: Nebraska concludes the season with the Black Friday finale with Iowa. Both teams enter the matchup looking to end the regular season on a high note.
content: Nebraska concludes the regular season with its annual Black Friday finale against the Iowa Hawkeyes . Both teams enter the matchup fresh off a crucial win and now look to end the regular season with just one more. For the No. 25 Huskers, a win would earn them their first eight-win season since 2016 and could help them finish the year in the top 25. For the No. 13 Hawkeyes, a win would provide them a chance to compete in both the Big Ten Championship and College Football Playoff. But while this top-25 matchup presents opportunities for both sides, Nebraska’s still facing an uphill battle. Though they picked up a win over then-No. 14 Ohio State , the Huskers jumped on a few Buckeye slip-ups and had Memorial Stadium behind them. Now they head to Iowa City, where the Hawkeyes have remained dominant. Iowa’s only loss as a home team this season came to Ohio State 31-14 in early October. Though Nebraska just came off a win over the Buckeyes, it’s safe to say a lot has changed since the Hawkeyes faced them. Plus, Iowa’s got a lot of momentum coming into this contest. Iowa’s won its last four games, averaging 29 points and allowing less than nine points in that stretch. The Hawkeyes’ last win especially provided momentum. Iowa derailed Illinois 34-17 last week, shutting out the Fighting Illini in the second half, 17-0. Despite allowing over 300 passing yards on just 21 completions, the Hawkeyes generated two interceptions, including a pick-six. Iowa also suffocated Illinois’ run game, holding it to just 28 yards on 17 carries. Plus, Katin Houser did throw the ball 39 times, so the Hawkeyes’ defense overall played well. This is the brick wall Nebraska’s offense is dealing with. Though the Huskers scored 31 points against the Buckeyes, Iowa isn’t likely allowing that many points. But even if Nebraska finds success on offense, its defense is also in for a tough game. The Hawkeyes ran the ball 52 times for 263 yards and three touchdowns against Illinois and held possession of the ball for over 37 minutes. Iowa’s Hank Brown also threw 13-of-26 for 138 yards and ran for 32 yards and a touchdown on eight carries. The Blackshirts allowed Ohio State to score 28 points and Jeremiah Smith to rip them apart. Though it generated two turnovers, those did just enough to get the win. Now, they get a well-spread Iowa group that rarely coughs up the ball. The win over the Buckeyes was big for Nebraska. But the Hawkeyes aren't a team that’s going to let a historic opportunity slip through their fingers. Unless the Huskers play perfectly in all three phases or catch a few breaks, Iowa’s bound to win this. title: Luke Moga Prepares for Second Start as Lobos Eye Mountain West Championship Hosting Rights
summary: ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. (KRQE) –The stakes are high for the University of New Mexico football team heading into Friday’s matchup against Air Force, and quarterback Luke Moga will be back under center for his second collegiate start. The Mountain West-leading Lobos can secure the right to host the Mountain West Championship Game with a victory over […]
content: ALBUQUERQUE, N.M. (KRQE) –The stakes are high for the University of New Mexico football team heading into Friday's matchup against Air Force, and quarterback Luke Moga will be back under center for his second collegiate start. The Mountain West-leading Lobos can secure the right to host the Mountain West Championship Game with a victory over the Falcons at University Stadium. Moga made the most of his first collegiate start, leading New Mexico to a road win over then-first-place Wyoming. He threw for 234 yards and a touchdown while adding another score on the ground. Despite the strong debut, Moga isn't satisfied with his performance. He's focused on improving his timing with receivers and making the most of every opportunity. "Yeah, I think just some timing things with guys, with receivers, and some things that I can do better," Moga said. "We can push depth on routes, so them expecting the ball and me putting it on them. There are some scramble opportunities. So every completion matters in this game." Moga also said he feels good about the team's progress heading into Friday's matchup, noting that the Lobos are getting players back healthier. Air Force will present another major challenge for New Mexico. The Falcons bring one of the Mountain West's top defenses to Albuquerque, allowing just 18.1 points and 273 yards per game. Air Force ranks among the nation's top five teams in passing defense and sits second in the Mountain West in that category. The Lobos will look to take advantage of home-field support while continuing their push toward a conference championship. Kickoff is scheduled for 2:30 p.m. Friday at University Stadium. title: Offensive Players to Watch as Tulane Gears Up for South Florida Contest
summary: The Green Wave will look to end the regular season with a strong conference win.
content: The Tulane Green Wave will look to end the regular season on a high note as it takes on the South Florida Bulls on Saturday. The Green Wave hasn't had the season it wanted, but younger talent has shown that there can still be a bright future for the program. The team is coming off a 28-24 win over the North Texas Mean Green; though that victory came against a significantly hindered UNT team, Tulane still had to find a way to dig deep and battle from behind. The Wave now turns its attention to one final regular season test ahead of a potential bowl appearance. Here's a look at which offensive players could make the biggest difference for Tulane on Saturday. QB Trace Johnson As expected, Johnson has had some growing pains, but he had his best outing of the season last weekend against the Mean Green. The true freshman signal-caller completed 17 of his 21 pass attempts for 283 yards and four touchdowns, demonstrating poise and confidence as he led his team on a game-winning drive with just over two minutes remaining in the game. Johnson was named to the American Conference Weekly Honor Roll in recognition of his strong performance. There's no doubt that this kid has talent and can be the future of the program -- imagine just how much he can grow this offseason. For now, he's focused on capping off a freshman season that he'll never forget. RB Jaylin Lucas Lucas has been quiet since his hot start to the season, but he contributed in more ways than one against North Texas. The running back led all players with 46 rushing yards on five carries, but he also caught three passes for 79 yards and a touchdown. Lucas showed his versatility in a big way and continually put his team in position to succeed. What more could you ask for from a veteran player? It's vital that Lucas continues this momentum as he returns to the Sunshine State. Expect him to give it his all this weekend. TE Cameron Roberts Roberts came out of nowhere last weekend. The tight end has been quiet all season, but he put together an outstanding game with a team-high 81 yards and two touchdowns on four receptions. It was his best showing of the year by a long shot, and it couldn't have come at a better time. On top of this, Roberts is just a freshman -- he's got plenty of years of college football ahead of him. If last weekend was any indication of what Greenies can expect from him moving forward, well, then he has the chance to be a pivotal part of the offense for years to come.

title: Ohio State football Michigan hype video: 'FIGHT LIKE HELL'
summary: Ohio State dropped its Michigan-week trailer Thursday. Fire, legends, and one message: FIGHT LIKE HELL. The Game kicks off Saturday at noon on FOX.
content: It's here. The Ohio State vs. Michigan trailer dropped Thursday, right on schedule for game week, and it does exactly what a Michigan-week trailer is supposed to do. It reminds you what this game is. And it doesn't ask politely. Ohio State vs. Michigan trailer opens with fire and Buckeye legends The video opens with fire and sparks over helmets. Then the names start flashing across the screen. CJ Barnett. Nolan Baudo. Maurice Clarett. Ryan Day. Archie Griffin. Woody Hayes. James Laurinaitis. Mickey Marotti. Urban Meyer. Jim Tressel. That's the point, and the trailer doesn't hide it. This game belongs to the people who built it. From there it moves fast. Archival footage and recent highlights cut together -- hard hits, touchdowns, celebrations, crowd shots from both sides. The marching band. The Block O. Player close-ups. Campus landmarks. Historical photos. The whole thing is stitched together with voiceover that frames The Game as something bigger than a football game. "The greatest robbery in all of sport." "A vendetta of hatred." "Our culture versus their culture." "For the brotherhood." One line lands harder than the rest. The preparation lasts 364 days. The game lasts 60 minutes. The stadiums, the narration says, are cathedrals built with "blood, sweat, sacrifice." A countdown clock reads "THE GREATEST RIVALRY SINCE OCTOBER 16, 1897." Brick walkways are marked "HATE." And it all ends where it has to end, with three words on the screen and the Block O behind them. FIGHT LIKE HELL. Ohio State vs. Michigan: what the trailer means for Saturday Now, look. A hype video doesn't block anybody. It doesn't cover Jeremiah Smith . It doesn't fix a defense that gave up 31 points at Nebraska . But this one is honest about what Saturday actually is. Ohio State is 7-4. Michigan is 6-5. There is no Big Ten title on the line. There is no College Football Playoff berth on the line. There is only the rivalry, and in this rivalry, that has always been enough. The Buckeyes won in Ann Arbor last year, 27-9, snapping a four-game losing streak in the series. A win Saturday would give Ohio State back-to-back wins over the Wolverines for the first time since 2018-19, and it would do it at home, at noon, in front of a Horseshoe that has been waiting all year for this one. That's what the trailer is selling. Not a playoff run. Not a trophy. Just the game itself, and the 364 days that go into 60 minutes of it. Watch the trailer, then get ready. Saturday can't get here fast enough. title: Tennessee's Arion Carter, DeSean Bishop remain questionable vs Vanderbilt
summary: Tennessee football running back DeSean Bishop and linebacker Arion Carter remain questionable against Vanderbilt.
content: Tennessee football running back DeSean Bishop and linebacker Arion Carter remain questionable against Vanderbilt. Bishop and Carter were listed again on the SEC student-athlete availability report on Nov. 26. It will be updated daily and finalized 90 minutes before the game. No. 7 Tennessee (9-2, 6-2 SEC) must beat Vanderbilt (4-7, 1-7) in the regular-season finale on Nov. 28 (7 p.m. ET, ESPN) to solidify a College Football Playoff spot. Bishop, a Heisman Trophy candidate and Doak Walker Award finalist, suffered a lower-body injury in a 27-13 win over LSU on Nov. 21. He left the game and did not return. Bishop, a former Karns High standout, leads the SEC in rushing with 1,215 yards along with 13 touchdowns. His 248 rushing attempts are second most in the nation. Carter, a former Smyrna High standout, suffered a lower leg injury in a 27-13 win over LSU on Nov. 21. He leads the team with 76 tackles, along with 11 tackles-for-loss, five sacks and three fumble recoveries. Eleven Tennessee players have suffered season-ending injuries in 2026: starting wide receiver Mike Matthews (knee); starting guard Nic Moore (undisclosed medical condition); starting defensive end Tyree Weathersby (knee); starting guard Wendell Moe (lower leg); starting safety Edrees Farooq (knee); starting tight end Ethan Davis (knee); running back Daune Morris (broken leg); safety Dylan Lewis (foot); wide receiver/kick returner Joakim Dodson (leg); linebacker Jaedon Harmon (knee); and cornerback Jadais Richard (upper-body). The initial report is released on Wednesday of an SEC game week, with daily updates leading to a final report 90 minutes prior to kickoff of a Saturday game. Prior to game day, players are designated by their school as available, probable, questionable, doubtful or out for the upcoming game. On game day, they are designated as available, game-time decision or out. Here’s what those designations mean: • Out: Will not play, 0% chance to play. • Doubtful: Unlikely to play, 25% chance to play. • Questionable: Uncertain to play, 50% chance to play. • Probable: Probable to play, 75% chance to play. Per SEC policy, schools must accurately designate players’ participation status. If the school has knowledge that a player may not be able to participate in the upcoming game for any reason (injury, illness, suspension, ineligibility or personal matter), it must report it. Failure to do so will subject schools to potential penalties ranging from $25,000 for a first offense to $100,000 for a third and further offenses. title: Utah RB Wayshawn Parker gets notable injury upgrade for West Virginia game
summary: Utah football running back Wayshawn Parker faced brief odds in playing against West Virginia . But that changed quick on Thanksgiving. content: Nov. 26—GRAND FORKS — UND forward Josh Zakreski missed four months last season after a practice injury required leg surgery. Zakreski was in and out of the lineup early this season, but landed on UND's top line Saturday night. Zakreski spoke to the Herald about his recovery and shared some of his off-the-ice favorites. Q. Coach Dane Jackson said Saturday night that your injury lingered into the summer and you were unable to skate a lot. What was your summer like? A. I didn't skate from basically when we lost to Wisconsin (in April) until when I came back here in July. I took a lot of time off to try to give my ankle some rest. It seemed to have helped, but I kind of got behind other guys on the team. I've been try to work as hard as I can, skating a lot, getting into the gym and trying to catch up. It kind of seems like I've started to catch back up slowly, so I've been feeling really good on the ice. I'm just kind of excited where I'm going, trending in the right direction. Q. What did it feel like Saturday night on a line with Cole Reschny and Mac Swanson? A. Playing with Resch and Swanny was awesome. Just getting the opportunity to play with those guys. . . they're such gifted hockey players. It was a tight game, but I felt like I played my role well. Q. You beat out a couple of icing calls Saturday. Did it feel like you were playing fast? A. I felt like I had some good momentum. My legs felt really fresh, even though we played Friday. But I felt good out there. I was just trying to use my speed and play my game and play how I was last year before my injury. Q. Why did you start playing hockey? A. Definitely my dad. I started late. I didn't start playing until I was 7 or 8. I was playing floor hockey before. That's what got me into it. I started to enjoy it. Then, my dad put me in skates and I've been in it ever since. Q. If there's one current or former hockey player you could have dinner with, who would you choose? A. This is going to be a weird one, but I'd say Tyson Kozak. I used to room with him in Portland, so I think it would be good to get back and have a nice dinner with him, catch up and see how he's doing. Q. What are your pregame rituals? A. I like to take a nap, for sure. I like to get a good pregame meal in, shower, pretty basic. I would definitely say when I get to the rink, I have a pretty big superstition where I just like to focus on talking to myself and doing a little bit of breath work and visualizing what's going to happen on the ice. Q. What's the most memorable goal you've ever scored? A. I'd say double OT against Everett in the playoffs my last year in Portland. We ended up beating them and they were the top-ranked team in the league that year, so that was my most memorable, for sure. Q. What game was it? A. Game 4. We were down 2-1 in the series. We tied it up, then went to Game 7 of that series and ended up beating them. Q. What's something you're competitive in besides hockey? A. Probably golf. My golf game got a lot better this summer. I was able to shoot my first 80. I almost shot 79, but blew it on the 18th hole. I'd definitely say golf. I'm really starting to get into it. Q. What's your dream vacation spot? A. Somewhere over in Europe like Greece or Italy. . . just somewhere cool I've never really thought about going, somewhere I can enjoy and take a break. I like the food in Italy, so that would be a big one. Q. What's your favorite meme? A. I don't use a whole lot of memes, so I'm not sure I can answer that one. Q. What's your favorite childhood memory? A. Probably playing baseball. My dad and I would always go work in the baseball cages. I managed to hit two home runs in one game, and it kind of taught me that hard work really does pay off. I loved playing baseball growing up. Q. What's the best food spot in Grand Forks? A. I really like that Joe's Italian place. You also can't go wrong with Harry's. Q. If you had to sing karaoke, what would be your go-to song? A. Mr. Saturday Night by Jon Pardi. Q. What's the best meal your mom or dad cook? A. My dad can cook up some good burgers. My mom makes this spaghetti pie. I really like that. She whips up some good pierogies, too. Q. What's your favorite part about your hometown, Saskatoon? A. I'd say seeing my friends and family. I don't get to see them a lot.

title: Cricket Australia widens 'Sandpapergate' forum to 2017-2018 Ashes
summary: Cricket Australia widened its independent "Sandpapergate" forum on Friday to include the preceding Ashes series against England, while pledging to make the findings and its response public.In a surprise development, the terms of reference released Friday broadened to include "ball-management practices" during the 2017-2018 season, including the home Ashes series which Australia won 4-0.
content: Australian fielder Cameron Bancroft (R) is questioned by the umpires after using sandpaper in the third Test against South Africa in 2018 (GIANLUIGI GUERCIA) Cricket Australia widened its independent "Sandpapergate" forum on Friday to include the preceding Ashes series against England, while pledging to make the findings and its response public. The governing body has ruled out reopening its investigation into the explosive 2018 ball-tampering scandal in South Africa that blew up again this month. Instead, it proposed a forum for players, coaches and staff on the tour to share their versions of events. In a surprise development, the terms of reference released Friday broadened to include "ball-management practices" during the 2017-2018 season, including the home Ashes series which Australia won 4-0. The hosts' consistent ability to get reverse swing in that series had England's bowlers scratching their heads. In the wake of the South Africa fallout, England great Alastair Cook, who was part of the Ashes side, was asked whether the team suspected Australia of ball-tampering. "Yes a little bit, certainly in Perth when the outfield was wet with rain they got the ball-reversing," he said. The issue went no further. Experienced senior counsel Fiona McLeod will lead the forum, which will be open for six weeks and is voluntary. Players' accounts, which can be written or verbal, will be confidential. She will investigate the Ashes, all four Tests of the South Africa tour, the events of March 24, 2018, when Cameron Bancroft was caught with sandpaper, and the conduct of the 2018 Cricket Australia probe. McLeod will provide a report detailing the principal themes and her recommendations. But what players say will not be published, no new sanctions will come out of it and she is not charged with determining any individual responsibility. "This is an opportunity to provide their accounts in a safe environment and to provide the CA board with relevant information including about the events of that tour and resultant investigation," said Cricket Australia interim chairman David Boon. "We are acutely aware of the enormous toll the renewed focus on this tour eight years ago has had on those involved and their welfare remains our main priority. "This forum is the best opportunity for people to speak and be heard, and for CA to listen and learn," added Boon. "Publishing the report in full is part of our commitment to transparency, and to be open with cricket fans about what we learn. It is also very important to understand that it will not seek to sanction or recriminate." - Reignited - The issue was reignited this month by Usman Khawaja, who claimed in his autobiography that the whole team knew about the plot to alter the ball with sandpaper during the third Test in Cape Town. He also claimed the practice was used in the second Test at Port Elizabeth. A Cricket Australia probe at the time concluded only skipper Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner and Bancroft were in the know. They were sent home in disgrace and banned for between nine and 12 months. Khawaja's version of events was backed by Warner and Bancroft, but strenuously denied by current captain Pat Cummins and fellow bowlers Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood. The bowling group at the time -- which also included Nathan Lyon -- released a joint statement in 2021 denying any involvement. Cricket Australia last weekend said Cummins had their "unanimous support" to remain Test captain and rejected any suggestion his integrity had been compromised, while praising him for changing the culture of the team. Australia are preparing for four Tests against New Zealand, starting in Perth on December 9. mp/pst

title: 'One bad day for us': Tilak Varma admits India A's bowling let them down after Sri Lanka A's stunning chase
summary: After their defeat to Sri Lanka A, India A's captain Tilak Varma shared his frustration regarding the bowling effort. Though the team posted an impressive 317 runs, it wasn’t enough as Sri Lanka A chased it down, thanks to centuries from Lasith Croospulle and Sineth Jayawardene. Varma encouraged the bowlers to reflect on their performance while praising the debutants' contributions, hoping the team will learn and emerge stronger next time.
content: NEW DELHI: India A captain Tilak Varma admitted that his side's bowling failed to deliver when it mattered after a crushing eight-wicket defeat to Sri Lanka A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars semifinal on Thursday. Despite putting 317 on the board, India A were knocked out after Sri Lanka A chased down the target with 9.3 overs to spare, powered by centuries from openers Lasith Croospulle and Sineth Jayawardene. Calling it “one bad day” for his side, Tilak credited the Sri Lankan batters but acknowledged that India A would need to introspect on their bowling after failing to defend a challenging total. “Yeah, credit goes to them. Both the openers played really well. But at the same point again, I was trying all the bowlers, but one bad day for us. I couldn’t get any help. But it’s fine. One odd bad day, but credit goes to Sri Lankan batsmen,” Tilak said after the match. The India A skipper also felt that the batting unit had done well throughout the campaign, while identifying bowling as an area that needed attention. “If you see as a batting group, we have done really well. But I think in bowling, we’ll go into the dressing room or go back home and introspect things, and we’ll come back stronger,” he added. 'We haven't executed': Tilak on India A's failed bowling plans India A had hoped that 317 would be enough to put Sri Lanka A under pressure, particularly with the pitch expected to slow down as the innings progressed. Tilak revealed that the plan was to keep the scoring rate in check during the first 15 overs and make batting more difficult later. “Yeah, I was telling my boys that initially the first 15 overs will be very crucial. If we restrict them to anything six per over, it will be very good for us. Later on, the wicket gets slightly slower side. That’s what we planned, but unfortunately we haven't executed,” he said. Tilak believed India A had a competitive total after recovering from a middle-order wobble, with Shahbaz Nadeem and Tanush Kotian adding valuable runs towards the end. “Honestly, we thought that around 320, 330 will be a good score on the board. But, you know, the wicket was slightly slow after the 20 overs. Initially, first 20 overs, it was nicely coming onto the bat. But after that, slightly slower side. Few balls were gripping and staying low. So, but there again, we got like three wickets back to back we got out. So after that, coming back to Tanush and Shahbaz, the way they played, and 318 (317) was good on the board,” he said. Sri Lanka A openers dismantle India A attack India A's plans unravelled almost immediately as Croospulle and Jayawardene made the most of early reprieves. Jayawardene hammered 105 off 70 balls, while Croospulle scored 116 off 107, the pair adding 174 for the opening wicket to take the game away from India. Nishan Madushka remained unbeaten on 58 and shared an unbroken 53-run stand with Pavan Rathnayake (31 not out) to complete the chase at 318 for two in 41.3 overs. Earlier, Abhishek Sharma's 78, Tilak's 53 and Sooryavanshi's 40 gave India A a flying start. But after the top order lost momentum, Nadeem's unbeaten 54 and his 73-run partnership with Kotian helped lift the total to 317 for eight. Tilak also highlighted the positives from the campaign, pointing to the contributions of debutants and the depth they brought to the side. “Yeah, it is really positive things. You know, there are so many youngsters who have first time playing, especially Shahbaz and Tanush. Tanush himself has debuted and also Shahbaz. You have seen he has handy bowling and also he can bat down the order. It’s really positive thing. And also Tanush, he’s also an allrounder coming back again,” he said.

title: What Did Formula 1 Drivers Think of the FIA's Surprise Kahoot Quiz in Qatar?
summary: Formula 1 drivers sat down with the FIA’s stewards in Qatar on Thursday, November 26, for their yearly talk about racing rules, and the governing…
content: Formula 1 drivers have their say after the annual meeting with the FIA stewards in Qatar. (Source: @evrythngformu1a/X) Formula 1 drivers sat down with the FIA’s stewards in Qatar on Thursday, November 26, for their yearly talk about racing rules, and the governing body turned it into a game. With drivers teed up to give answers on multiple choice questions via their phones, the FIA ran through a host of incidents that had taken place over the year, asking each driver what penalty they would have given. It’s an odd sight, a room full of the world’s fastest drivers tapping answers into a classroom quiz app. Kimi Antonelli , the newly crowned champion, came out of it happy. The Mercedes driver said “most of us in the room were all aligned” on the incidents they watched, and that the session helped the stewards “to see how we see certain scenarios”. The FIA held its annual meeting with Formula 1 drivers and stewards in Qatar on Thursday to review controversial incidents and penalties from the 2026 season. This year, the meeting took an unusual approach, with the FIA using Kahoot! to present multiple-choice questions about… pic.twitter.com/PX4Ov1RVgN — | ⁶³ | Kris | (@krisg7gr63) November 26, 2026 Max Verstappen agreed, telling reporters “It’s good to do that,” because it let stewards hear “our voices of what we think a penalty should be”, according to The Race . The turnout had its own storylines. Fernando Alonso was unwell and Lance Stroll chose not to attend, while Lewis Hamilton showed up after skipping the meeting the previous year. The seven-time champion was blunt about it: “I didn’t go last year but I’m going to go tonight, yes.” How the FIA Turned a Rules Meeting Into a Game The setup was simple. Options included different time penalties or no sanction, and drivers voted on each clip. Some of the incidents triggered unanimous agreement from drivers and stewards over the punishment handed out, while others left opinion more divided. Kimi Antonelli and Max Verstappen were happy with how the stewards’ meeting went. (Source: MEGA) The FIA had a clear reason for doing it this way. The format was meant to let drivers give more candid opinions than they might voice openly, and to show that some incidents are not clear-cut. Frankly, it’s a smart move: a driver who won’t criticize a rival’s penalty in front of 19 peers will happily do it with an anonymous tap. Antonelli said the split votes proved a point. Some cases are “so borderline that it’s so hard to establish who is at fault”, he said, and in those moments the call should “just need to be a racing incident and no penalty.” Antonelli believes Formula 1 drivers should just give back the position if they overtook off the track. (Source: MEGA) That fits a mood that had been building all week, and the real talk soon turned to what happens next. Formula 1 Drivers Push for Quicker Fixes on Corner-Cutting Before the meeting, Oscar Piastri had questioned where the penalty system was heading, saying some decisions looked especially harsh while others arguably warranted stronger action. Still, nobody walked out demanding a rewrite. No major rule changes were called for next year, though some change may come on track-limit advantages gained by cutting corners. Lewis Hamilton believes Formula 1 can improve a lot when it comes to policing on-track action. (Source: MEGA) Antonelli wants the fix to be fast. On drivers who cut a corner to pass, he said the best move is to “just tell the driver to drop the position straight away”, adding “if you give straight the position back is more fair as well.” Another idea on the table was a new sanction that would drop a driver from a guaranteed position at the end of a race, instead of a time penalty. Hamilton framed his return as a chance to “help the racing be better and the ruling system I’m sure we can improve.” Verstappen was more realistic about who holds the pen. After the drivers have their say, he said, “of course they make their minds up and they decide what they’re going to do next year”. That’s the catch with any feedback session. The votes are counted, but the drivers only find out if anyone listened the next time a steward’s decision lands on them in the heat of a race.

title: Hamilton reveals if he and Leclerc are still free to race after Las Vegas clash
summary: Lewis Hamilton has confirmed that he and Charles Leclerc remain free to race each other in the final two rounds of the season, despite their controversial collision at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The two Ferrari drivers were involved in several wheel-to-wheel battles throughout Sunday's race in Las Vegas, with their fight eventually resulting in contact.
content: Lewis Hamilton has confirmed that he and Charles Leclerc remain free to race each other in the final two rounds of the season, despite their controversial collision at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The two Ferrari drivers were involved in several wheel-to-wheel battles throughout Sunday's race in Las Vegas, with their fight eventually resulting in contact. Hamilton was sent into a spin following the collision with his teammate, while Leclerc subsequently received a 10-second time penalty for causing the incident. The seven-time world champion eventually crossed the finish line in seventh place, while Leclerc had to settle for tenth, bringing an already difficult weekend for the Maranello-based outfit to a disappointing conclusion after both drivers failed to progress to Q3 on Saturday. The incident prompted a strong reaction from Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur, who immediately requested a meeting with Leclerc over the team radio after the chequered flag. The Frenchman subsequently expressed his frustration with how the situation between his two drivers had unfolded. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Hamilton confirms freedom to race Leclerc Speaking to Sky Sports F1 ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, Hamilton confirmed that Ferrari did not impose any new restrictions on its drivers, reiterating that avoiding contact remains their primary responsibility. “We're still free to race, and I think that's the ultimate goal of being here. We want to race, but of course we don't want what happened last week to ever happen.” Hamilton also reiterated that avoiding collisions between teammates had always been the number one rule at Ferrari, rather than a new instruction introduced following the events in Las Vegas. The Briton went on to discuss the outcome of his conversation with Leclerc in Qatar, having previously revealed details of their latest private talks earlier on Thursday: “Charles and I had a good sit-down earlier on and had our chat. And I think moving forwards, I think we can be fine.” Hamilton plays down intensity of Ferrari tensions Despite the events in Las Vegas and the subsequent scrutiny surrounding Ferrari's driver pairing, Hamilton insisted that he and Leclerc enjoy competing against one another. The seven-time world champion also suggested that the situation between the two Ferrari drivers appears considerably more intense from the outside than it actually is behind closed doors. “We do enjoy racing together and we do have a really good relationship. It's obviously intense. On the outside, it seems a lot more intense than it really is.”

title: Alabama basketball freshmen take step forward in Las Vegas vs Kansas State
summary: Alabama basketball bounced back against Kansas State with the help of its freshmen. How the rookies gained Nate Oats' trust in Vegas.
content: Alabama basketball rediscovered its offensive rhythm in Las Vegas, although putting Kansas State away proved more difficult than building a comfortable lead. After dropping its Players Era Festival opener to Baylor, the Crimson Tide bounced back with a 104-91 victory over Kansas State on Thursday, Nov. 26, at T-Mobile Arena. Here are three takeaways from No. 15 Alabama 's Thanksgiving win. IN THE PROS: Alabama basketball alum Labaron Philon puts NBA on notice, earns praise from LeBron James RECAP, HIGHLIGHTS: Alabama basketball holds off Kansas State in Vegas Qayden Samuels making case for Nate Oats to keep him on the floor After Kansas State (3-4) took its first lead of the night, Samuels needed just 27 seconds to knock down consecutive 3-pointers and put Alabama (6-1) back in front. As valuable as the non-starter's perimeter shooting was, his ability to stay involved when shots weren't coming his way was just as important. Samuels needed seven first-half minutes to score 12 points and finished with a team-high 14 on just three field-goal attempts, converting all eight of his free throws while grabbing six boards on the night. "That's about as efficient as you can get," Oats said. Although five turnovers illustrated where there's still room for growth, Samuels was among four freshmen Oats trusted to help close out the game and three who finished with double figures. "I wanted to keep some of the veteran guys' minutes down," Oats said. Amari Allen, Aden Holloway prove stability Crimson Tide needs early There were moments when it seemed like Alabama could use Allen or Holloway to take over the game, and while the offense eventually found its footing, it may not have if not for its most experienced ball-handlers. Allen got bigs involved early, finding Kentucky transfer Brandon Garrison for two baskets before setting up Boise State transfer Drew Fielder for a dunk. Later, Holloway helped NC State transfer freshman Cole Cloer find his rhythm from beyond the arc, assisting on a pair of 3-pointers in a 29-second span. Despite combining for just 11 points themselves, the returning duo accounted for 10 of Alabama's 12 first-half assists. Their willingness to share the ball helped seven Crimson Tide players reach double digits and gave Oats the luxury of subbing out Allen with four minutes to play and Holloway with 9 1/2 minutes remaining ahead of Friday's meeting with Miami. Alabama still learning how to put teams away As encouraged as Oats was by Alabama's defensive effort against Baylor, Thursday showed how easily the Crimson Tide can undermine its own progress. Kansas State shot just 33% from the field in the second half but still managed to score 56 points. Alabama's 21 turnovers yielded 20 points for the Wildcats. Even when the Crimson Tide forced missed shots, Kansas State extended possessions by grabbing 13 offensive rebounds in the second half and generating 15 second-chance points. Factor in the Wildcats' 24 made free throws after halftime, and it's easier to understand why Oats came away encouraged by Alabama's defense itself, although frustrated with its discipline. "If we clean those up, I thought we had an outstanding game defensively," Oats said. Emilee Smarr covers Alabama basketball and Crimson Tide athletics for The Tuscaloosa News. She can be reached via email at esmarr@usatodayco.com. This article originally appeared on The Tuscaloosa News: Alabama basketball freshmen take step forward in Las Vegas vs Kansas State

title: Arkansas basketball loses to Michigan State but makes progress
summary: Arkansas didn't get a quality win, but the Hogs seemed to grow up
content: Arkansas basketball lost another game to a power conference opponent on Thursday. The Razorbacks dropped a 70-67 thriller to Michigan State in Detroit. The end result isn't good, but to be quite honest, this was a real step forward for John Calipari's team. It's absolutely true that moral victories are not the point of competition , and that a team with Sweet 16 and maybe Elite Eight potential is still behind schedule for the season, given the lack of high-end wins on its resume. However, given how bad this team looked against Virginia and Indiana, the performance against Tom Izzo's team should be encouraging for John Calipari and his staff. It no longer seems that Arkansas is hopelessly and substantially lost as a team. The defense was a lot better against Michigan State than it was against Indiana. This team needs to be good at the defensive end of the floor in order to be a real contender in the SEC, and the defensive performance on Thanksgiving moves the needle several notches in the right direction. Arkansas forced 13 Michigan State turnovers and blocked 5 shots. Michigan State did shoot over 50 percent, but it wasn't as though the Spartans were getting to the rim with regularity. Michigan State shot the cover off the ball from 3-point range, going 8 of 12. Most opponents aren't going to shoot that well with such a small sample size. Arkansas' effort in this game was excellent. The Hogs collected 17 offensive rebounds to just 7 for Michigan State. Arkansas began to look like the hungry team we hoped it would be before the season began. Michigan State prides itself on hustle and toughness. Arkansas matched Michigan State in that regard, a big sign of growth and evolution for the young Razorbacks. John Calipari really seemed to get through to his young guys on the need to play every possession with passion and forget the previous play. Arkansas was more mature and more forwardly-focused in this game. The players are beginning to understand what it takes to win... but they're not quite there. As good as the effort was for Arkansas, the inability to finish plays is hugely frustrating for the Razorbacks. They hit just 3 of 23 3-point shots. They made only 10 of 16 free throws. Jeremiah Wilkinson and Billy Richmond were a combined 1 for 14 on threes. Arkansas gained Wilkinson in the transfer portal specifically for his offense. As we have said before, if Wilkinson isn't making shots, he's a net negative for this team. Arkansas - which seemed like a deep team on paper before the season began - got just 2 points and 5 rebounds from its bench in 36 total minutes. Arkansas doesn't have the eight- or nine-deep rotation which was supposed to wear down opponents with smothering, constant energy. The better overall performance against Michigan State came from the discovery of the best starting five so far this season, with Davion Thompson starting and Miikka Muurinen going to the bench, two moves we thought Calipari needed to make. The starting five appears to be set, but now the bench needs to give Arkansas a lot more production. The Hogs improved, but now they need to finish off important games against high-quality opponents. It's time to start building an NCAA Tournament resume. Arkansas isn't in a state of full-blown crisis, but the Razorbacks have to start winning the most significant games on their schedule. They can't continue to swing and miss as December arrives.

title: Wes Enis' 20 points help Creighton beat TCU 95-87

content: LAS VEGAS (AP) — Wes Enis scored 20 points, including five during a decisive late-game stretch, and Creighton beat TCU 95-87 on Thursday in the Players Era 16. The Bluejays (6-1) advance to Friday’s bracket championship against the winner of Baylor and No. 22 Gonzaga after scoring at least 90 points in two straight games for the first time since November 2024. TCU (5-2) erased a nine-point halftime deficit and led 81-80 with 3:43 remaining. Enis answered with a 3-pointer 26 seconds later and added a jumper with 2:32 left to give Creighton an 85-83 lead it never surrendered. Brock Harding converted a three-point play to pull TCU within 87-86 with 1:43 remaining, but Jasen Green blocked Harding’s layup on the Horned Frogs’ next possession. Green made two free throws, and Hudson Greer scored with 42 seconds left to push the lead to 91-87. BJ Davis added 17 points for Creighton, while Greer scored 13 off the bench. Jackson McAndrew and Austin Swartz each had 11. Harding finished with 19 points, 10 assists, seven rebounds and four steals for TCU. DJ Thomas scored 17 off the bench, and Micah Robinson added 13 points and seven assists. Creighton shot 55% from the field. Up next TCU: At Notre Dame on Dec. 5. title: Why Rick Barnes says Braeden Lue is on 'monster' run for Tennessee in Las Vegas
summary: Rick Barnes said senior forward Braeden Lue has been "a monster" for Tennessee basketball as it continues rolling defensively with a win vs. Iowa State.
content: LAS VEGAS − In its two wins at the Players Era Festival, Tennessee basketball has held top scorers Pharrel Payne, who entered the tournament averaging 19.6 points per game for Maryland , to five points, and Trey Singleton, averaging 18.6 points for Iowa State, to eight. And after the Vols dispatched the Cyclones with more suffocating defense at Michelob ULTRA Arena on Nov. 26, sophomore forward DeWayne Brown II said there’s one reason why even those talented forwards struggled to put the ball in the basket. “We put B-Lue on ‘em,” he said. “B-Lue” is Braeden Lue, the 6-foot-8, 243-pound transfer from Kennesaw State who logged eight rebounds, three blocks, a steal and more solid individual defense that went beyond the box score as No. 11 Tennessee (7-0) won 75-64 against Iowa State (4-2) on Nov. 26. By beating Iowa State, the Vols have advanced to the third round of the Players Era Festival, where they'll meet the winner of No. 13 St. John's vs. No. 23 Louisville on Nov. 27 (9 p.m. ET, ESPN). A win over the Red Storm or Cardinals would send them to the event's championship game on Nov. 28 (10:30 p.m. ET, ESPN). Lue was an important reason why the Vols dominated defensively against the Cyclones, holding them to 30.6% shooting, the second-lowest by a Tennessee opponent this season, and 0.928 points per possession. “Tremendous,” Tennessee coach Rick Barnes said. “Lue just gives us that physicality. He competes. He's put together a run here four or five games where he's just been really a monster for us on the glass and doing the dirty work. “And he can defend. … We hope he can continue to build because we think he'll be able to guard anybody on the court eventually.” In only 19 minutes per game this season, Lue has excelled at finishing possessions with a defensive rebound, something Tennessee has struggled mightily to do consistently. And he has become a tone-setter for the strong defensive performances which have powered the Vols’ seven-game winning streak that opened this season. “He’s just a junkyard dog. He’s an everyday guy. He knows his role. He knows what he has to do to get us to the next level and he’s really answering that challenge right now,” sophomore guard Jalen Haralson said. “So he’s a guy that we can switch at the four, on smaller guards, big guys. He’s a junkyard dog.” In two preseason exhibitions and the first three games of the regular season, the Vols looked incapable of meeting the high defensive standards Barnes has set during his tenure as coach. Now, they are on a roll, playing a brand of defense that more closely resembles successful Vols teams of the past. Tennessee has allowed opponents to shoot only 26.9% from the field and score 56.5 points per game during a four-game stretch that began with the record-setting victory over Michigan State in Knoxville on Nov. 17. “I think what happened (in the exhibition) at Duke was probably the best thing that ever happened to us, because in that game, we just thought we were just going to shoot the ball and we got embarrassed,” Barnes said. “And after that, we've been on an uptick and we've got a chance to be so much better, too.” Lue’s counting stats during this stretch have been modest - two points, 4.5 rebounds and 0.75 blocks over 18 minutes per game. But his teammates and Barnes insist that Lue has been as crucial to the team’s early success on defense as anyone. Brown is far from surprised with Lue’s steady contributions, because this is what the Vols get from him all the time. “He’s basically doing what he does in practice every day,” Brown said. “He’s just translating it to the game.” Stephen Thompson covers Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball. title: Dodgers Sign Utility Man Eric Wagaman To Minor League Deal
summary: The Dodgers added depth with Eric Wagaman. See his stats, the contract details, and what this means for the roster in this quick breakdown.
content: Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Dodgers made their first move of the free agency period by signing veteran utility man Eric Wagaman. According to Francys Romero of Beisbol FR, the agreement constitutes a minor league contract including a spring training invitation. This comes as the team has not added any big names to the roster yet. The signing happens just before an expected lockout that will pause most team operations. Wagaman brings experience from the New York Mets, Miami Marlins, and Minnesota Twins. He is 29 years old and can play first base, third base, or the corner outfield spots, according to Sports Illustrated . While he did not make the Opening Day roster last year, he has seen time in the big leagues with three different clubs. He made his debut with the Los Angeles Angels in September 2024 after being selected in the Rule 5 draft. That season, he appeared in 18 games and hit two home runs with a .673 OPS. Even though his batting average was .250, he showed he could be a reliable bat off the bench or in a starting role. His journey was not a straight line to success. He started with the New York Yankees in 2017 but never reached the big leagues there. He moved to the Angels, then the Marlins, and finally the Twins before landing with the Mets. In New York this past season, he struggled a bit, hitting .191 in 26 appearances. He was designated for assignment and then elected free agency. This move shows he is willing to fight for a spot again. He knows what it takes to stay in the game. Smart Roster Depth for the Future The minor league deal is a low-risk move for the Dodgers. Since he is not on the 40-man roster, he can still talk with the team during the lockout. This gives him a head start when camp opens. He will have a chance to impress the coaches and earn a spot on the big league team. Santiago Espinal’s 2026 actions mirror this situation. title: Marlins Need Imanaga After Sánchez Deal, Not Just Any Veteran
summary: The Marlins signed Gary Sánchez to a one-year, $6.5 million deal. Now the front office must target Shota Imanaga to fix a rotation that lacks depth.
content: Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images The Miami Marlins finally made a move this offseason by agreeing to terms with catcher Gary Sánchez on a one-year contract. A person with knowledge of the talks told The Associated Press the deal could be worth up to $6.5 million. No position player has ever received a larger contract from Peter Bendix, the president of baseball operations, in his tenure. Sánchez, who turns 34 next week, spent last season with the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers. He hit just .209 for the title-winning club but posted a much better .801 OPS against left-handed pitching. The Marlins struggled mightily against southpaws last year, ranking 27th in wRC+ and posting an 85 wRC+ in that category. Sánchez brings a right-handed bat to a lineup that desperately needs to hit lefties better in 2027. Signing Sánchez fixes a specific hole, but it leaves the rotation wide open for a major upgrade. The front office cannot stop there if they want to build on an 80-win season. Sandy Alcantara remains the ace, and Eury Pérez showed flashes of brilliance despite an up-and-down year. Max Meyer is expected to be ready for spring training after a neck injury cut his season short. Beyond those three, the depth is thin. Janson Junk and Ryan Gusto proved serviceable, while Tyler Phillips struggled with home runs after joining the rotation. The team needs a left-handed starter who can eat innings and keep runners off base. Robbie Ray or Matthew Boyd could work as one-year stopgaps, but they are not the long-term answer. Why Imanaga Is The Missing Piece Shota Imanaga is the name the Marlins should chase to complement their young core. He has posted season ERAs of 2.91, 3.73, and 3.77 in his three seasons stateside. His ability to limit traffic on the bases is elite, with a 1.038 WHIP that ranks sixth-lowest among 36 pitchers with at least 80 starts since 2024. Fish On First reported that Imanaga has been a quality starter despite concerns about his tendency to give up the long ball. Preventing walks becomes his greatest strength when he keeps the ball in the park, with walk rates ranking in the 97th, 96th, and 95th percentiles. Preventing walks is exactly what a young rotation needs to stay out of trouble early in games. The Defense Factor And Roster Math While Sánchez offers offensive help, his defense remains a liability. He graded out as a below-average defensive catcher, recording negative six blocks above average and negative two framing. This is why the team added three catchers to the 40-man roster, including Joe Mack and Agustín Ramirez. Sánchez will likely DH or serve as a late-game pinch-hitter against left-handed pitchers. The Marlins might utilize him at first base to enhance their defense, where he has recorded a minus-one DRS. The signing gives the team a veteran presence in a young clubhouse, but it does not solve the starting pitching gap. To become legit contenders, the Marlins must immediately focus on addressing their rotation. Jeff Passan of ESPN reported the agreement on Wednesday night, setting the stage for the next big move.

title: Marlins Outfielder is Generating Trade Interest
summary: Teams around Major League Baseball may want to make serious offers for Miami outfielder Kyle Stowers
content: The Miami Marlins may have another difficult offseason decision on their hands, and this time it involves one of the most productive players in their lineup. Outfielder Kyle Stowers is reportedly generating interest from several clubs, sending rumors swirling that the team may trade him this winter. For a franchise continuing to build toward sustained contention, Stowers represents an interesting asset. He has demonstrated the ability to provide legitimate power in the middle of a lineup, but his growing value could also make him an attractive trade chip as the Marlins evaluate their roster and long-term organizational priorities. The interest is hardly surprising, and president of baseball operations Peter Bendix has taken notice. Stowers enjoyed a breakout 2025 campaign, batting .288 with 25 home runs and 73 RBI in 117 games. However, his 2026 season wasn't quite as impressive, but it shouldn't be overlooked. The youngster hit .239 with 21 home runs and 65 RBI while posting a .789 OPS, which were still solid numbers. Unfortunately, injuries have become a significant part of the conversation surrounding Stowers. He missed the first 21 games of the 2026 season with a hamstring injury, then another hamstring issue and an abdominal strain that limited him to 121 games. There is also the financial component to consider. Stowers is entering his first season of arbitration eligibility, with his 2027 salary projected to be around $3.2 million. He remains under team control through 2029, giving an acquiring club multiple seasons of relatively affordable production. Why Would Miami Trade Him? The Marlins have made it clear that their intention is to become competitive in 2027. After finishing 80-82, the organization is looking to take another step forward rather than dismantle the roster. At the same time, Miami also has several areas that need attention, particularly its pitching staff. If another organization presents an attractive package featuring controllable starting pitching or high-end prospects, Peter Bendix would have to at least consider the possibility. The Marlins have also reportedly explored adding a starting-caliber player at a corner infield or outfield position. Depending on how those discussions develop, Stowers could become somewhat expendable, particularly if Miami identifies an opportunity to improve multiple areas of its roster through a trade. Stowers is only 28, has demonstrated legitimate middle-of-the-order potential, and already has experience producing at an All-Star level. Finding a replacement via free agency could be considerably more expensive, and there is no guarantee that an outside acquisition would provide an upgrade. Unless another club makes an offer that substantially exceeds what Miami believes Stowers can provide over the next several seasons, keeping him might be the smarter baseball decision. In the end, the team must decide if some of the prospects in the organization, like rising star Dillon Lewis , could replace Stowers. Then, the more experienced and (somewhat) established player could be used as a commodity for pitching or perhaps some corner infield help. In that scenario, Bendix would have to pull the trigger. So, in many ways, it may be less about Stowers' ability and potential, and more about the teams needs and the talent the depth they have in the organization. This potential trade comes down to that type of numbers game.

title: Too Early to Panic About A's Lack of Moves This Offseason
summary: The Athletics finished with one of the worst records in MLB in 2026 and are one of the few teams that are still worse than they were when the offseason began. With more ground still to make up, it's still too early to panic about 2027.
content: Since making the first trade of the offseason, the Athletics have been fairly quiet this offseason, stacking up players on minor-league deals, but not adding a ton of impact talent to the big-league roster just yet. Teams like the Colorado Rockies have been adding pitching before the expected lockout, but the A's have stayed put. The A's lack of movement so far this winter is illustrated in this table, where each team's projected WAR change since the start of free agency is ranked. Of course the New York Mets, who signed Tarik Skubal, are at the top of the heap. The A's, meanwhile, are one of just seven clubs to have not had a positive impact this offseason. Projected WAR Change Since Start of Free Agency pic.twitter.com/7mn1WaEkRo — Thomas Nestico (@TJStats) November 26, 2026 The A's rank 27th on this list with a -1.5 WAR, and while the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays rank 26th and 29th, they're also starting from a much higher point, while the A's are being left further behind. Only the Angels (62-100) and Rockies (58-104) finished with worse records than the A's 64-98 mark, but the Angels rank 21st on this table, while Colorado is astonishingly 2nd. Of course, it's still early in the overall offseason, but with the lockout set to begin on December 2, this first phase of the offseason is going to wrap up shortly. Don't Panic Just Yet While the A's haven't been active, it's still too early to panic about the team's outlook for 2027. The first reason is that there are still a few days before baseball shuts down, and there will be some time before the start of the season when free agents who are still on the market can be wooed, or trades can be made before Opening Day 2027. The other and arguably bigger reason is that the A's new front office has mentioned numerous times that development is going to be a big area of emphasis for them moving forward, and we've seen some of that at work already as the club now has president of baseball operations Taylor Smith and GM Cam Castro splitting the duties that used to be held by just David Forst. They've also hired new hitting and pitching coaches, as well as directors of both hitting and pitching to make sure the A's philosophy is preached up and down the system. With a focus on limiting walks and generating more ground balls next season, the pitching staff should be improved even with the same pitchers on the staff, thanks to the new philosophy and some of the new information that will be shared with them. The A's may not have made a huge addition to the roster just yet, but getting more out of guys like Gage Jump, Jacob Lopez and Jack Perkins would be a huge boost to the club's pitching performance in 2027.

After spending two seasons without a true righty-hitting option at catcher, the Yankees still are searching for Austin Wells’ complement. “If we can find a good-defending, right-handed-hitting option to level up, that’d be great,” Yankees general manager Brian Cashman said earlier this month at the GM Meetings, “but that’s also slim pickings.” The pickings are even slimmer now. The one catcher still on the free-agent market likely to command a multiyear and not-insignificant contract is Carson Kelly. It is likely that the caliber of catcher the Yankees add will depend upon their pursuits of bullpen, center field and third base help. If they land reliever Adrian Morejon, for example, they probably would reach into the bargain bin elsewhere (unless they bring in a catcher through trade). With less than a week to go before signings and trades are expected to freeze, here are some of the righty-hitting catcher options who are still available through free agency: Carson Kelly: The best still on the board, Kelly likely expects more playing time and a better contract than the Yankees are willing to give. But a veteran, well-regarded catcher with a lifetime .822 OPS against southpaws would fit well. Austin Hedges: One of the premier framers in baseball, the 34-year-old always has been defensively excellent but not much of an offensive threat. Last season, he did hit lefties well (.747 OPS). title: Dricus Du Plessis: If the Adesanya I fought shows up at UFC Riyadh, Magomedov 'done for'
summary: Dricus Du Plessis expects Israel Adesanya to rebound at UFC Fight Night 295.
content: Dricus Du Plessis expects Israel Adesanya to rebound at UFC Fight Night 295. Former champion Adesanya (24-6 MMA, 13-6 UFC) takes on rising middleweight Shara Magomedov (17-1 MMA, 6-1 UFC) in the Dec. 5 main event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Adesanya will look to snap a four-fight losing skid – one of the setbacks which came in a title fight against Du Plessis at UFC 305 . Although Adesanya hasn't been getting his hand raised, he has shown shades of his championship form, and that's what Du Plessis is banking on. "It's an awesome fight, and once again with Adesanya, that's what's so great in his whole career: He's not shying away from anything," Du Plessis told Fight Forecast . "He's still taking those hard fights. 'Bullet' is an up-and-coming killer. I honestly believe Adesanya, I hope for him, and I just believe he's going to be too much for Shara because Shara 'Bullet' can do great things and he can strike, but if the Adesanya that fought me gets in there, Shara 'Bullet' is done for. Adesanya, he changed teams, so he's going to have a chip on his shoulder. "He went to go and train with (Alexander Volkanovski), and we've seen what Volk has been doing. That team has been really shaping up so, big ups to Adesanya. At the end of his career, he doesn't need to fight these killers and to change the gym now at this age and at the end of his career. He doesn't have to do that. But he's such a martial artist, he wants to be the best he can be, and the fact that he does that shows me that he's still committed to winning, not just competing. I'm excited for it, and I'm going with Izzy for that one." Adesanya parted ways with his longtime gym, City Kickboxing, to train in a more concentrated environment at Unity MMA. Du Plessis was asked if the UFC still needs Adesanya. "Right now he's almost in that Anderson Silva time in his career, at the end where Anderson was losing fights, but nobody cared," Du Plessis said. "His legacy was already cemented. He's done what he's needed for the sport, and right now I don't think the UFC needs him. I think fans love him, fans love his style, and I think he loves the sport, so I don't think it's the UFC needs him anymore. "I think he loves it so much he needs it more – not that he needs it. He needs it for himself. He loves it so much that he feels empty without it. I think that's how a lot of us feel. ... I think if he gets that big, big win, I think maybe even this fight he might call it a day. But up until, let the man fight. Let him enjoy his life because it's not like he's getting manhandled, and he's fighting the best in the world."
