title: Champ Kyle Larson is On a Generational Run. Could Others Catch Up?
summary: Kyle Larson is on as close to a generational run as you can get in the current era of the NASCAR Cup Series with the NextGen car but could others catch up?
content: Kyle Larson is on as close to a generational run as you can get in the current era of the NASCAR Cup Series with the NextGen car. Larson is a three-time Cup Series champion and the winner of the last two championships, becoming the first back-to-back series champion since Jimmie Johnson won five in a row from 2006 to 2010. The highlight of Larson's season was undoubtedly his Chase run. He scored three wins, six top-five finishes, eight top-10 finishes and an average finish of 7.3 in the final 10 races. He led 579 of the 3,151 laps he completed and scored 456 points, 54 points more than any other driver. Going into the final race, Larson had an average finish of 6.78. He had four consecutive top-two finishes after the Chase opener that allowed him to basically be in control in the second half and locked it up with an actually generational win at Talladega Superspeedway. Larson and crew chief Cliff Daniels proved they're their own type of animal on another level from their competitors and trying to knock on the door of Jimmie Johnson and Chad Knaus. Now, back up three months and imagine telling someone this -- like the publisher and editor here at NASCAR Roundtable. At the end of August, confidence in Hendrick Motorsports winning the championship was slim but not zero for a reason. Larson scored no wins, nine top-fives and 13 top-10s in the first 26 races. Although they showed they weren't far off in one metric, leading 659 of the 6,328 laps they completed in the regular season, they had an average finish of 17.3. They started the Chase in the No. 7 seed, one position below the effective cutoff teams declared preseason and 55 points out of the lead. Indianapolis, Chicagoland, Nashville Superspeedway and EchoPark Speedway Atlanta in the spring all represented different times where Larson missed the mark as a driver. Yet, when the Chase started, it was game on for Larson and everyone else looked relatively semi-pro in retrospect. Has everyone caught onto their game? Maybe. Drivers like Christopher Bell, Denny Hamlin, Chase Briscoe and Ryan Blaney all could've been hoisting the Cup if one or a few little things had gone differently. Larson earned the championship with performance that was not only stellar but clean. For instance, Hamlin earned 40 or more points just once in the final nine races, while Larson did it six times. Larson didn't need to start that well because a stellar run in the Chase got them there but not every season will present that. A new Ford body is coming, Chevrolet is in its second year with a new body and Toyota's body is well-seasoned to make 2027 a challenge.

title: What New Rules Will NASCAR Have in 2027?
summary: NASCAR is making several changes, especially in the Cup Series, as 2026 ends and the 2027 season draws closer.
content: CONCORD, N.C. -- NASCAR is making several changes , especially in the Cup Series, as 2026 ends and the 2027 season draws closer. NASCAR issued a bulletin to teams Friday, Nov. 20, detailing the changes. Here are the highlights, according to what NASCAR sent the media: For the NASCAR Cup Series intermediate engine package, the horsepower level will be elevated from 670 to 750 starting at Charlotte-1. The All-Star Race will feature a horsepower level of 800 hp. After that race, NASCAR and the engine builders will do a full analysis on the race quality and engine performance. If the industry feels comfortable, NASCAR may increase to 800 hp for all Cup Series short tracks and road course starting at Bristol-2. Though not part of the Rule Book bulletin, NASCAR will implement a NCS qualifying-specific setup for Daytona and Talladega qualifying with the goal of reaching 200 mph laps. Splitter stuffers will be removed at all short tracks and road courses in the Cup Series. NASCAR has removed rules for minimum damper length in the Cup Series, giving teams further setup options. Except for the Daytona 500, if Qualifying is incomplete, the current Team Owner Points standings will be used to assign starting grid positions. Superspeedway qualifying sessions will move to one round, only. Updated wet-weather oval procedures: Once the Race has started and NASCAR has declared wet weather conditions, the crew chief will determine any tire configuration changes. NASCAR added the following language to the double painted line rule to further clarify the rule: NASCAR defines beneath the double painted lines as follows: When the vehicle’s left side tires are beneath the left line of the inside double painted lines that separate the apron from the racing surface. NASCAR clarified the rules around a driver missing a race without NASCAR approval: Before The Chase, the affected driver and/or Team owner will begin The Chase with 2,000 Points. All other qualified drivers and/or Team owners will retain the reset Points totals corresponding to their respective standing position as outlined in Table 12.4.2 Driver and Team Owner Points Adjustment. During The Chase, the affected driver and/or Team owner will have their respective Points totals reset to 2,000 Points. For the NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series, the driver/owner would reset to 2,020; in the NASCAR FedEx Freight Truck Series, the reset would be 2,030. NASCAR adjusted the minimal engine seal count: Teams considered to be full-time (i.e. entered in all Events for the current Race season) must compete in a minimum of 20 Points Events with a sealed engine during the Race season. An L3 penalty option has been added to the NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series and NASCAR FedEx Freight Truck Series.

title: 5 Potential Destinations For Deni Avdija When He Inevitably Hits Free Agency In 2028
summary: Deni Avdija's contract is one of the most team-friendly in the NBA, but it's also surely going to lead to him hitting unrestricted free agency in 2028.
content: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Portland Trail Blazers have exceeded expectations at the start of this 2026-27 NBA season. The Trail Blazers are sixth in the Western Conference with a 12-6 record, and it’s Deni Avdija who has led the charge. Avdija emerged as an All-Star for the Trail Blazers last season and has carried on from where he left off. The 25-year-old is averaging 24.9 points, 6.6 rebounds, 6.1 assists, 1.1 steals, and 0.4 blocks per game while shooting 51.9% from the field and 43.3% from beyond the arc. That’s terrific production from a player who is notably in the third year of a four-year, $55 million rookie scale extension. This is quite a bargain for the Trail Blazers, but it is also a double-edged sword. You see, extensions are capped at 140% of the salary in the final year of the existing deal. Avdija will only make $11.8 million in 2027-28, so there is virtually no chance he agrees to an extension in 2027. The Trail Blazers can renegotiate and extend up to his max, but that would require them to shed a lot of salary to create cap space, a route they’re unlikely to go down. So, Avdija will almost inevitably hit unrestricted free agency in 2028. You’d think the Trail Blazers could just offer him the super max to keep him, but he isn’t eligible for it no matter how well he plays from here on out. The Trail Blazers officially acquired Avdija from the Washington Wizards in July 2024, which meant he was already in his second contract when he got traded. That makes him ineligible for the supermax. This is quite a situation that the Trail Blazers find themselves in, and here we take a look at five potential options for Avdija when he becomes an unrestricted free agent. 1. Portland Trail Blazers Now, of course, the likeliest outcome is that Avdija chooses to return to the Trail Blazers, who have his bird rights. The Israeli has repeatedly spoken about how much he loves Portland, and he is now also leading a team that can make noise in the West. Back in the offseason, the Trail Blazers were called a “sinking ship” that Avdija probably should leave in free agency, but they clearly aren’t looking like one now. If they are a playoff team in 2028 as well, he wouldn’t have to look elsewhere to be in a situation where he can play winning basketball. The Trail Blazers can also offer Avdija a five-year deal with 8% yearly raises in 2028, while other teams can only put four-year deals with 5% yearly raises on the table. He will have made $75 million in salaries when this current deal expires, which is a lot of money, but more financial security wouldn’t hurt. 2. Golden State Warriors Should things go south for the Trail Blazers in 2027-28 ( Damian Lillard and Jrue Holiday are 36), Avdija could be tempted to look elsewhere. The Golden State Warriors would be one of the teams in position to pounce. As of now, the Warriors are expected to have cap space to pursue a max player in 2028. Stephen Curry ($60.1 million) and Brandin Podziemski (20.5 million) are currently their only players set to make over $10 million in 2028-29, and the former has a player option. Going to the Warriors would mean Avdija gets to lead the post-Curry era along with Podziemski and Yaxel Lendeborg . They have a lot of draft picks they could trade to further improve that roster as well. Also, if Avdija cares, he’d be in one of the biggest markets. 3. Boston Celtics Now, the Boston Celtics aren’t projected to have a lot of cap space in 2028, but they’re going to need a co-star for Jayson Tatum . They, of course, traded away Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers this past offseason for Paul George . George has surpassed expectations so far, but he is 36 years old and has a $56.6 million player option for 2027-28. You’d imagine the Celtics would prefer he opt out and sign a multi-year deal at a lower annual rate, but we don’t know what his intentions are. Whatever George does, he is not going to be on the Celtics’ books for $50 million in 2028. With the way Derrick White is shooting , it might be in their best interests to ship him out of town in the next year or so as well. White has a $34.8 million player option for 2028-29, and if the Celtics do manage to move off him without taking on long-term salary, they could have space for Avdija. He and Tatum would ensure they remain contenders for the foreseeable future. 4. Dallas Mavericks Going to the Dallas Mavericks would see Avdija team up with another former Duke star in Cooper Flagg . The Mavericks should have plenty of cap space in 2028 as well, but this does depend a bit on what a potential Kyrie Irving extension looks like. It won’t be difficult for them to create space, though. With Flagg already looking like a superstar with averages of 24.3 points, 6.3 rebounds, 6.7 assists, 1.8 steals, and 0.8 blocks per game as a sophomore, the Mavericks would be an intriguing landing spot for free agents. He already has them ahead of schedule, as they are right behind the Trail Blazers with an 11-7 record. It’s undoubtedly a team on the rise. 5. Memphis Grizzlies Speaking of exceeding expectations, no one has done that to the extent that the Memphis Grizzlies have. The Grizzlies are fifth in the West with a 14-5 record. While 29-year-old Ty Jerome has led the charge, this is a team with a lot of young talent like Cameron Boozer , Cedric Coward, and Zach Edey . The Grizzlies are only going to get better as time passes, and they will likely have cap space to get Avdija and elevate themselves even further. The only issue here, though, is that those Grizzlies youngsters are going to be up for significant extensions in the coming years. You can only have so many players on large contracts in this second-apron era, so they might have some reservations. Memphis has never been a popular free agent landing spot either, so Avdija might have some reservations as well, making this the least likely of the five destinations.

title: What the Lakers need to do to reach the NBA Cup knockout round
summary: There are several scenarios in which the Lakers would advance to the knockout round of the Emirates NBA Cup.
content: The Los Angeles Lakers will have a big test on Friday when they visit the San Antonio Spurs to start a difficult three-game road trip. While they have the NBA's best record at 15-3, San Antonio is right behind them at 15-4. Friday's game will also be the final NBA Cup group play contest for both teams. It could very well decide which team wins West Group C, although the picture is a bit more complicated than that. For the Lakers to win the group and guarantee themselves a spot in the knockout rounds of the Emirates NBA Cup, they will have to defeat the Spurs and the Portland Trail Blazers will have to beat the Golden State Warriors on Friday. Right now, all four teams are in a tie for first place in West Group C with a 2-1 record in group play. Los Angeles defeated Portland 124-118 on Nov. 6 in group play, giving it the tiebreaker over Portland, but it lost to the Warriors in group play on Oct. 30. The Lakers have to win on Friday to advance to the knockout round. But if they win and the Warriors prevail over Portland, things will become murky. NBA Cup West Group C Friday scenarios: Lakers win group if: - Lakers win at San Antonio AND - Portland wins at home vs. Warriors Getting the West wildcard would be tough for LA at 3-1 given their -9 point differential relative to DAL/DEN (Group A) and MIN/MEM (B) (below): pic.twitter.com/YSS5qRVGO2 — Mike Trudell (@LakersReporter) November 26, 2026 The Lakers are at the bottom of that four-way tie in West Group C with a -9 point differential. That puts them at a disadvantage, as point differential is a major determinant of which team gets the wild-card spot in the knockout round. The three group winners and one wild card in each conference advanced to the first knockout round, which will start on Dec. 4. If the Timberwolves (3-0 in group play) defeat the Memphis Grizzlies (2-1) on Friday, that would leave the Denver Nuggets (2-1) as the one team L.A. would have to beat out. If the Nuggets then lose to the Utah Jazz , Los Angeles would be in. If the Nuggets win, Los Angeles would have to have a higher point differential than the Nuggets, who are currently at -3. A Grizzlies victory would mean that L.A. would have to finish ahead of the Timberwolves. That seems unlikely, as the Timberwolves have a +39 point differential. title: 10 Eagles things I think I think after incredible comeback vs. Cowboys
summary: One of the most improbable wins in Eagles history.
content: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 26: Joe Milton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles walks off the field with the Madden Thanksgiving MVP trophy after an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Incredible. There’s no other way to describe the Philadelphia Eagles’ comeback victory over the Dallas Cowboys — which was way more enjoyable than any meal you could consume on Thanksgiving. This is an Eagles game that’s going to be remembered forever, just like the Christmas Day win over the Cowboys in 2006 and the Miracle at the Meadowlands comeback in 2010. The victory is that improbable, especially when the Eagles were down 31-10 with 3:35 left in the third quarter. They had no business being in this game, yet they found their way back to make it a game — and stole a victory away from the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. This was a game the Cowboys should have won handily. Instead they choked it away, thanks to the hands of a resilient Eagles team that didn’t let their 3-7 record stand in the way of what seemed to be an insurmountable deficit. No matter how the rest of this season goes, that was one heck of a win. This victory will be talked about amongst generations of Eagles fans. A Thanksgiving miracle — that may have ended the Cowboys season. The Eagles are good at ruining seasons all of a sudden. 1. What else can you say about Joe Milton? Milton delivered one of the greatest performances my a quarterback in Eagles history. What Milton did against the Cowboys was absolutely incredible, and this was more than a quarterback showing off his ridiculous arm talent. The final stat line: 21-of-31, 311 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT, 10.7 YPA — 121.8 rating. 3 carries, 15 yards, TD. There are only two quarterbacks in Eagles history with 300+ passing yards, 3+ passing TD, 1+ rushing TD, and average 10+ YPA in a game — Milton and Michael Vick (2010 at Commanders). That’s how well Milton played on Thanksgiving — in just his third career start. Once the Eagles trailed 31-10, Milton went 11-of-16 for 181 yards with 2 TD, 1 INT and a 120.1 rating (averaging 11.3 YPA). He also had 15 yards and a rushing touchdown in that stretch to bring the Eagles back from three scores. This level of play was throughout the game. Milton used his arm strength to keep the Eagles offense moving, going 11-of-19 for 278 yards with 3 TD, 1 INT and 14.6 YPA on throws that traveled 10+ air yards — finishing with a 120.1 passer rating. He was 2-of-6 for 95 yards and 2 TD with 0 INT for a 121.5 passer rating on throws that traveled 25+ air yards. Any completion on passes that traveled 25+ air yards was a touchdown. The Eagles had some exciting performances from Jalen Hurts over the years, but that was arguably the most exciting passing performance by a quarterback since Nick Foles threw for 471 yards against the Houston Texans in 2018 (and that was an Eagles’ win too). Impressive performance by Milton, finally giving life to an Eagles offense that badly needed it. 2. The most impressive feat of Joe Milton’s day? Milton had a touchdown pass that traveled 64.4 yards in air distance, and that wasn’t the most impressive aspect of his performance. He threw an interception into triple coverage with 7:14 to play when the Eagles were trailing 38-3, which seemed to be the backbreaker with how the defense was playing. The Eagles got the ball back and Milton goes 4-of-4 for 70 yards and a 24-yard touchdown to Makai lemon on the ensuing drive — netting a perfect 158.3 passer rating. The poise and ability to forget that interception immediately following the interception spoke more volumes about who Milton is as a player than anything else he accomplished on Thanksgiving. When Milton made a boneheaded play, he responded in the way winning quarterbacks respond. He hasn’t even been on his team for two months and was able to shake that play off and perform at an even higher level. Since the interception, Milton finished 6-of-9 for 84 yards with a touchdown and a 133.6 passer rating. He led the Eagles to victory with a touchdown drive and set Jake Elliott up with his game-winning field goal. Want to know how to stick around as a starting quarterback in the NFL? Moments like that. 3. Joe Milton might have locked up QB2 One of the few things I wanted to see in the remainder of the season was if Milton could play well enough to be the QB2 next year. Judging Milton through two starts was tough, given the state of the offense and the changes the Eagles were making to accomondate his game. Milton didn’t get to throw the deep ball much, and he missed when he had his opportunity last week to DeVonta Smith. He didn’t miss any of those opportunities on Thanksgiving, hitting two of them for 95 yards and two touchdowns. On throws that traveled 20+ air yards, Milton went 6-of-11 for 188 yards and 3 TD with 0 INT — a 139.2 passer rating. The arm strength was clearly on display, along with the accuracy on the deep ball. Milton was relentless facing pressure too, finishing 7-of-10 for 154 yards with 3 TD and 0 INT for a 152.1 passer rating — while also being sacked five times. He was 6-of-8 for 145 yards with 3 TD and 0 INT on throws from outside the pocket — 156.3 rating. Backup quarterbacks don’t have games like this. QB5’s — which is what Milton was when he signed — really don’t have games like this. This performance may have locked up QB2 for Milton next year. If Milton can stack up good-to-solid performances, he’ll be the QB2 on the Eagles (at least). Milton may get a starting opportunity elsewhere too (he is a restricted free agent), but the Eagles can control his fate there as well. The situation needs to play itself out, but Milton is certainly on the radar around the league. He’s earned it. 4. That victory had to be bittersweet for Joe Milton When Milton was making incredible throws against the Cowboys, I couldn’t help but think of his journey to get to this point. Over the last four months, Milton was cut by the Cowboys after losing the QB2 job to Sam Howell —toiling on the practice squad for five weeks. Any team could have claimed Milton when he was waived, and no team did. Any team could have signed Milton from the Cowboys practice squad to the active roster, and no one did. The Eagles signed Milton to the active roster when Jalen Hurts was lost for the season due to blood clots in his lungs. If Hurts wasn’t done for the year, the Eagles wouldn’t have brought in Milton. He literally was their QB5, the fifth quarterback to make the active roster. Tanner McKee got three starts before the Eagles turned to Milton, Andy Dalton told the Eagles he had a better opportunity with the Atlanta Falcons. Milton wasn’t considered by the Cowboys and 31 other teams until the Eagles needed a quarterback. To have a performance like that against a team that cut him and chose Sam Howell over him had to be bittersweet — especially since he led the Eagles to a 21-point comeback on the road against that team on Thanksgiving in just his third start. Certainly Milton will soak that all in at some point, but the battle to succeed and have a moment like that are why sports are so great. Even when Milton was counted out, he wasn’t. 5. Legendary performance from DeVonta Smith There were questions whether DeVonta Smith was a WR1 earlier this season. There shouldn’t be any following Thanksgiving. Smith finished with 11 catches for 200 yards and two touchdowns in the win over the Cowboys, the first Eagles’ player to get 200+ receiving yards in a game since DeSean Jackson in 2010. He had the most receiving yards on Thanksgiving since 1945 — and the second-most by any player on the holiday in NFL history. Smith had two touchdown catches of 45+ yards, the first player to do that on Thanksgiving since Randy Moss in 1998. He had more receiving yards on Thanksgiving (200) than A.J. Brown has the whole season (128). How good was the Milton-Smith connection? Milton was 11-of-14 for 200 yards with 2 TD, 0 INT and a 158.3 passer rating when targeting Smith — 14.3 yards per attempt. He hit Smith on throws of 24, 50, 45, and 23 yards of those 11 completions, and also hit him six times on throws of 10+ air yards. When Smith is healthy, he’s very good. He wasn’t even fully healthy in this one, injuring his lower back trying to make an insane catch in the fourth quarter on a Milton deep ball. Smith could barely run at full speed the rest of the way, yet still was able to go out and make plays. Smith has 42 catches for 551 yards and 4 TD in six games. He’s averaging 91.8 receiving yards per game, a 17-game pace of 1,561 yards. With the injuries, Smith is still on pace for 851 receiving yards (and those numbers will go up if he’s good enough to play). Milton has an excellent chance to stick around with Smith on the field. That connection was brilliant on Thanksgiving. 6. The Eagles play hard for their coach Hard to state the claim the Eagles have given up on Nick Sirianni based on the last two games. A win against the Pittsburgh Steelers to end a seven-game losing streak is a gut-check victory. Stealing a game on Thanksgiving against the Dallas Cowboys is in unchartered territory. The Eagles were down 21 points with 3:35 left in the third quarter. They had eight plays in the quarter that went for 1 yard at that point, while the defense allowed 31 points on seven possessions and 6.7 yards per play. They could have packed it in and allowed Dallas to continue to roll. They didn’t. The Eagles not giving up in a season that has experienced injury after injury (including the multiple starters that left the game), team captains and long-time starters getting traded, the handling of Jalen Hurts’ blood clots, and the uncertain future of the coaching staff speaks volumes of how Nick Sirianni prepares his team during the week. No matter what Sirianni does during a game (and after), his players are still playing for him. The message is still getting across to the players in that locker room and the Eagles don’t believe their playoff chances are dead yet. If Sirianni is back after this season, this is the reason why. This locker room has no checked out on him, and they are demonstrating that with their performance on the field. Any team could have called it a day down 31-10 late in the third quarter. Not the Eagles, who had their biggest comeback in 16 years. 7. About that Nick Sirianni postgame fan interaction I understand why Sirianni acts like he does. Sirianni is a very emotional individual and a competitor who puts his heart and soul into coaching. Going on a seven-game losing streak took its toll on Sirianni, who spent weeks trying to figure out what was going on with his football team. This is a head coach who was 59-26 (.694 win percetatge) after his first five seasons, making the playoffs all five years and winning a Super Bowl while appearing in another one. Sirianni is fighting for his team — and his job. The last two months have been brutal. The Eagles head coach gets caught up in the moment with fans a little too much. He lets his emotions get the best of him. I’m not even sure if he was interacting with Eagles fans or taunting Cowboys fans, but it was enough where he had to be pulled away by Dom DiSandro. Sirianni shouldn’t be putting himself in that situation, and he’s done it far too much. I like that he’s authentic, but that is taking it too far. The Eagles head coach shouldn’t care what the fans think of him, good or bad. It’s clear Sirianni hears what’s said of him and acts on it when he wins. Sirianni gets over the top with this stuff, a silly distraction after the massive win. The Eagles have enough issues to worry about inside the Jefferson Health Training Complex. 8. Jake Elliott — stone cold Can’t speak enough on how good Jake Elliott has been all season. Elliott’s two field goals on Sunday were the reason the Eagles won, and he gave the Eagles their first lead of the game on a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left — and the kick would have been good from 65 yards. Elliott had ice in his veins when making that kick, just like the majority of clutch kicks he’s made in his career. Elliott is 14-of-14 on field goals in the final minute of a game in regulation or overtime, 5-of-5 on kicks of 50+ yards in one-score games. He’s 2-for-2 in those situations this season, and 1-of-1 on game-winning field goals. Elliott has improved to 5-of-5 on 50+ yard field goal attempts, after being 5-of-15 (33.3%) on those kicks over the previous two seasons. Elliott is 8-of-9 (88.9%) on 40+ yard kicks this season after going 20-of-34 (58.9%) on those kicks over the previous two seasons. The comeback is incredible, and why the Eagles chose to adamantly defend Elliott this offseason. Just an amazing season from Elliott, who might be in line for an All-Pro campaign. 9. Hats off to Ty Robinson This Eagles comeback doesn’t happen without Robinson, who made the most of his opportunity when his number was called. Robinson had three pressures in seven pass-rushing snaps, an insane pressure rate of 42.9%. One of those pressures was the fourth-down sack on Dak Prescott on 4th-and-1 with 55 seconds left — the first one of Robinson’s career. This was a player who wasn’t even guaranteed to make the roster once training camp started, and earned his way onto this team with his play in training camp. That play set the Eagles up to steal the game, and set off a fire in Dallas on whether Brian Schottenheimer should have punted or went for it — enough where his job is in question. Robinson was able to make that massive of a presence as a pass rusher, and deserves more playing time going forward. Oh, and Robinson also blocked a punt that was recovered by Kenny Moore for a touchdown. That play was massive in the Eagles’ comeback, and cut the deficit to 31-24 with 13:53 left in the game. Robinson should have been credited with a forced fumble in this game too, but I digress. Robinson is the first player in Eagles history to record a sack and a blocked punt in the same game. This is a player that logged just 73 defensive snaps this season prior to Thursday. The Eagles have something with Robinson. They traded Jordan Davis for multiple reasons. 10. It was nice to see this team move the ball in the second half The Eagles entered this game with the worst second-half offense in football. The 4.6 point average in the second half was last in the NFL. So was the yards per play (3.6), average yards in second half (110.1), and net yards per attempt (4.3). The only major statistic that wasn’t 32nd was yards per carry — 30th at 3.3. This week was significantly different. The Eagles scored 22 offensive points in the second half (29 total), averaging 6.9 yards per play and gaining 200 yards of offense. They averaged 5.4 yards per carry and 8.5 net yards per attempt — all this while only converting 20% of third downs. This was the worst team in football in the second half, and they’re still last in the league in offensive points scored (6.2), yards per play (3.9), and average yards in second half (118.3). yards per carry moved up to 29th (3.4) and net yards per attempt improved to 31st (4.8). The Eagles even scored in the third quarter! Milton’s touchdown pass in the third quarter was just the second touchdown scored by the Eagles in the third quarter all season — the other one was against the Cowboys. They improved their third quarter scoring average to 30th in the league (2.1 points). This offense in the second half underwent a complete 180, and it didn’t start out that way (first eight plays went for a yard). Amazing turnaround once Milton hit Smith on that 45-yard touchdown with 24 seconds left in the third quarter. Can the Eagles build off this? Hopefully. Bonus: Enjoy this win (enjoy all of them). This is one the city of Philadelphia will talk about for a long time, even better since this season has been a disaster and this matchup seemed like a easy victory for the Cowboys (I didn’t even think the Eagles could score 20 points when I was watching Dallas film on Monday). You’ll remember where you were and who you were with when the Eagles pulled off this comeback. The Eagles are 4-0 against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving and Christmas — all games in Dallas. Happy Thanksgiving everyone!

title: Will Anderson Jr. Named AFC Defensive Player of the Week, Continues to Set the Tone for Houston
summary: The league-leading pass rusher dominated Indianapolis to secure his second career weekly honor, proving he is a generational centerpiece fueling DeMeco Ryans’ elite defensive transformation in Houston.
content: If there is one thing Houston Texans fans can appreciate about Will Anderson Jr., it's that the man understands the assignment. Being named the AFC Defensive Player of the Week is another indication that the Texans have something special in their young defensive end. But beyond the individual recognition, this award speaks volumes about what Anderson means to Houston's defensive identity and the culture DeMeco Ryans has been building. For me, Anderson receiving this recognition isn't necessarily a surprise. It's more of a reminder to the rest of the NFL that Houston has a legitimate defensive difference-maker who deserves to be mentioned among the league's elite pass rushers. Will Anderson Jr. is on top for the 7th straight week 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Mp0T1NkNSG — NFL (@NFL) November 24, 2026 Anderson Put the Colts on Notice Coming off Houston's dominant 26-3 Thursday night victory over the Indianapolis Colts, Anderson earned his second career AFC Defensive Player of the Week award after accumulating five tackles, four quarterback hits, two tackles for loss and a sack that resulted in his first career safety. The interesting thing about Anderson's performance is that the stat sheet doesn't necessarily tell the entire story. His presence alone disrupted the offensive rhythm of Indianapolis and made things extremely uncomfortable for quarterback Daniel Jones. Houston surrendered only 167 yards of total offense and 38 rushing yards. The Colts were held scoreless throughout the final three quarters. That's the type of defensive football Texans fans have been waiting to see consistently this season. Anderson was at the forefront of it. More Than Just a Pass Rusher What I appreciate most about Anderson is that he isn't a one-dimensional defensive end. Everybody loves seeing quarterbacks get slammed to the turf, but Anderson's ability to defend the run, collapse the pocket and force opposing quarterbacks into uncomfortable situations makes him extremely valuable. Through 10 games this season, Anderson has registered 44 tackles, 15 tackles for loss and a league-leading 11.5 sacks. He also leads the NFL with 60 quarterback pressures and a pressure rate of 19.3%. Those numbers are ridiculous when you consider the amount of attention opposing offensive coordinators have to dedicate to containing him. When Anderson commands additional blockers, opportunities open up for other members of the defensive front. That pressure also makes life a little easier for Houston's secondary. That's where his impact goes beyond individual statistics. Anderson makes the players around him better, and that's a characteristic you want from a franchise defensive player. Is It Time to Talk Defensive Player of the Year Why not? I think it's time we start having a more serious conversation about Anderson potentially bringing the NFL Defensive Player of the Year award back to Houston. According to the NFL, Anderson joins Von Miller and former Texans great J.J. Watt as the only players since 2000 to produce at least 10 sacks and 15 tackles for loss in three separate seasons before turning 26. That's some pretty impressive company. I'm not necessarily ready to start comparing Anderson's entire career to Watt's, but the trajectory is certainly encouraging. Houston has witnessed what a generational defensive talent can do for a franchise, and Anderson is beginning to establish his own legacy. The biggest factor moving forward will be maintaining that production while helping Houston climb back into playoff contention. Despite the inconsistencies surrounding the Texans this season, Anderson has remained one of the team's most dependable assets. My Two Pennies As a football fan, I thoroughly enjoy watching Anderson because his motor never seems to shut off. Whether he's fighting through a double-team, chasing down a running back or putting pressure on a quarterback, the effort is consistently there. Being named AFC Defensive Player of the Week is well-deserved, but I believe Anderson has his sights set on something much bigger. Now, it's up to the rest of the team to match that energy. Individual accolades are great, but watching Anderson lead this defense into the postseason would make his remarkable 2026 campaign that much sweeter. And quite frankly, I wouldn't be surprised if there's some additional hardware waiting for No. 51 when this season is all said and done.

title: Andy Reid didn’t like the refs overturning the late Rashee Rice catch
summary: The Bills beat the Chiefs, but one late replay review is under scrutiny.
content: Nov 26, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA; Buffalo Bills defensive back Amani Hooker (22) breaks up a pass intended for Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice (4) during the fourth quarter at New Highmark Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Gregory Fisher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Late in the Buffalo Bills win over the Kansas City Chiefs, a turning point in the game was decided by replay. On third down inside two minutes, Patrick Mahomes found Rashee Rice over the middle of the field and Rice was popped by Bills safety Amani Hooker. As he fell to the ground, the ball moved. On the field it was ruled a catch. Because it was inside two minutes, the replay official had to call for a review and not Bills head coach Joe Brady. After replay, it was ruled an incomplete pass. After the game, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid addressed the play, saying he didn’t like the call. “Not one that I agreed with,” said Reid of the replay review. “This came from New York,” Reid said. “They called it a completion. I’m not quite sure what they saw, I saw he had control of the ball, and his elbow hit then the ball hit, but he had control. Normally, in those kind of situations, it has to be clear obvious. To me that was not clear and obvious.” The NBC broadcast spent a lot of time on it during the game and again in the postgame. Rules analyst Terry McAulay thought it was a catch and the Chiefs should have moved the chains. Cris Collinsworth talked about the laces on the ball, and when Rice hit the ground his hand moved down those laces while the ball touched the turf. I think it’s pretty clear the ball moved. I think it’s pretty clear the ball hits the ground. You be the judge: WOW… Refs called this a catch on the field but after review overturned the call and ruled this an incomplete catch for the Chiefs… Very little movement on this ball to overturn that pic.twitter.com/5yZ6sMQqTr — Rate the Refs (@Rate_the_Refs) November 27, 2026

title: Bears, Eagles and Bills win as NFL serves up Thanksgiving thrillers
summary: Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze for a winning touchdown with three seconds remaining to lift the Chicago Bears to a 39-35 victory over Detroit on Thursday as all three NFL Thanksgiving games came down to the wire.Bears quarterback Williams's six-yard pass to Odunze -- who managed to get both feet down in the back corner of the end zone -- gave Chicago their first lead of the game in Detroit, where victory lifted them to 9-2 and into the NFC North division lead over the 8-3 Lions.
content: Chicago's Rome Odunze celebrates his game-winning touchdown catch with Bears teammate Kalif Raymond after the team's NFL win over the Detroit Lions (Gregory Shamus) Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze for a winning touchdown with three seconds remaining to lift the Chicago Bears to a 39-35 victory over Detroit on Thursday as all three NFL Thanksgiving games came down to the wire. The Buffalo Bills edged the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10 in a heavyweight AFC matchup thanks to a 57-yard Tyler Bass field goal as time expired. In Dallas, Philadelphia's Jake Elliott drilled a 59-yard field goal with two seconds remaining to give the Eagles a 39-38 victory over the Cowboys in a classic NFC East division clash. Bears quarterback Williams's six-yard pass to Odunze -- who managed to get both feet down in the back corner of the end zone -- gave Chicago their first lead of the game in Detroit, where victory lifted them to 9-2 and into the NFC North division lead over the 8-3 Lions. "We knew we needed a big one," Odunze said. "Luckily the O-line held up for me. Caleb delivered the ball exactly where it needed to be, and I was able to make a play in the back of the end zone." Williams connected on 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards and two touchdowns -- both to Odunze. The Bears had two rushing touchdowns from Kyle Monangai and one from D'Andre Swift to help offset a monster game from Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs, who ran for 205 yards and three TDs. The Bears erased an early 10-point deficit, knotting it at 10-10 on Monangai's first touchdown with 4:07 left in the first half. Jared Goff hit Sam LaPorta with an 11-yard scoring pass to push Detroit's lead to 19-10 going into halftime, but Monangai's two-yard TD had the Bears back within two, minutes into the third quarter. Gibbs motored 70 yards for a touchdown that gave Detroit a 35-24 lead with 8:20 remaining. Chicago responded with a three-play, 71-yard drive capped by Williams's 41-yard scoring pass to Odunze. Detroit came up empty on two possessions before the Bears put together their game-winning drive. - Marquee matchup fizzles - In Buffalo, cold, rainy weather put a damper on the marquee matchup between Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes and Bills counterpart Josh Allen. Allen connected on 10 of 21 passing attempts for 81 yards with two interceptions and no touchdowns. But James Cook ran for 117 yards and a touchdown and Bass booted a pair of field goals as the Bills improved their AFC-best record to 10-1 and the Chiefs slipped to 8-3. Mahomes threw for 174 yards, piloting a seven-play 56-yard drive capped by Emmett Johnson's one-yard TD run that put the Chiefs up 10-7 minutes into the second half. The Bills tied it on Bass's first field goal. Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker, who booted a 26-yard field goal in the first half, missed a 46-yarder with six minutes to play before Bass came through again. "I was just trying to stay fully present," Bass said. "Just telling myself: trust your preparation and go out there and soak it all in and have fun. "It was fun being able to do that for my team." - Milton's Eagles soar - The Eagles erased a 21-point third-quarter deficit to hand the Cowboys another heartbreaking defeat. Eagles quarterback Joe Milton threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another TD. Milton, claimed by the Eagles after he was cut from the Cowboys practice squad in October, said his meticulous work when he was still in Dallas had paid off. "You never know when your opportunity is going to come," said Milton, who was brought in to shore up Philadelphia's quarterback ranks after Jalen Hurts was lost for the season with blood clots. bb/pst

title: Ben Johnson goes viral for ‘Stanky Leg’ celebration shot at Amon-Ra St. Brown after Bears win
summary: The Chicago Bears head coach got the last laugh after Amon Ra St. Brown tried to make fun of his ‘stanky leg’ celebration during the Thanksgiving clash.
content: Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images The Chicago Bears head coach got the last laugh after Amon Ra St. Brown tried to make fun of his ‘stanky leg’ celebration during the Thanksgiving clash. Ben Johnson and the Chicago Bears faced off against his old team on Thanksgiving Day. The Bears have been flying high under Johnson’s leadership, but his offensive mind first came to the forefront with the Detroit Lions. As the offensive coordinator between 2019 and 2024 for the Lions, Johnson is quite familiar with a lot of their stars and best players. This includes star wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown. The Lions man and Johnson have both been integral to one another’s careers, but it seems there’s a bit of rivalry there too. St. Brown pulled out Johnson’s ‘stanky leg’ dance celebration during the game, but it was his former OC who got the last laugh at the end. NFL fans love that Ben Johnson gave it back to Amon-Ra St. Brown after the Chicago Bears won Chicago pulled off an incredible comeback during the game. Despite trailing 35-24 with just about eight minutes left in the game, the Bears offence managed to put up 15 points in that time to get the victory. Caleb Williams and Rome Odunze connected for two touchdowns, including the incredible game-winner. Johnson hadn’t forgotten that his former WR had copied his celebration earlier in the game either. While giving an electric postgame speech in the locker room after, he did the dance himself, shouting, “If you want a f****** Stanky Leg, you’ll get a Stanky Leg.” And fans absolutely loved it. “OWN HIM BEN, St. Brown is such a cornball,” one fan commented. “Everyone saying Amon-Ra and Ben are corny are dumb. Sports need more rivalries like this. I love the pettiness. It makes the game better,” a second fan claimed. “Nah ts hard cause the Lions were doing it all game lmao,” a third fan pointed out. “Yeah they’re winning it all this year. Electric energy from that whole entire team,” a fourth fan commented. “I love this guy and the Bears are not even my team,” a fifth fan said. “Everyone wants him as coach and Caleb as their QB… That’s why we hear so much hate,” a Bears fan wrote. Thanksgiving brought a lot of epic moments for NFL fans, and this was absolutely one of them. The NFC North is extremely competitive this season, and this win was massive for Chicago to claim the top spot for now. If these two teams meet once more in the playoffs, it would make for must-see TV. title: Chiefs’ Harrison Butker’s confidence is still high after latest miss
summary: Kansas City has trusted its longtime kicker through thick and thin this season.
content: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the fourth quarter of the Kansas City Chiefs ’ 13-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills , with six minutes remaining while the score was tied, kicker Harrison Butker took the field to attempt a 46-yard field goal. The potential redemption moment for the criticized kicker could have put Kansas City in front. Since missing a 51-yarder in perfect conditions at home against the New York Jets in Week 9, Butker has made all 18 kicks he’s been tasked with (three field goals and 15 extra points). Yet, this one was pushed right, just like it has on too many occasions this year. After the game, head coach Andy Reid was asked about Butker and potentially making a change at the placekicking position. “I’ll go back and go through all of it again,” Reid said. “But I’m not going to make any decisions right this minute.” Full postgame sound from #Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker following the loss to the Bills @KSHB41 pic.twitter.com/mTUQAjFsFk — Matt Foster (@MattFosterTV) November 27, 2026 In the locker room, Butker answered questions from reporters and faced the music. “Obviously, you want to do what you can to help the team, and I didn’t do that,” Butker acknowledged. “It’s a tough loss; I’m not happy with the result, and I’m not happy with the performance.” However, as a three-time Super Bowl champion and long-time professional athlete, Butker remained poised and continued to show ultimate belief in himself. “I think my confidence is always high,” Butker shared. “I just try to focus on the process and how I approach every kick. Obviously, you want them all to feel good, and I was hitting some good balls lately, the last couple of games; that miss just showed up again on that kick, unfortunately.” When asked about the potential impact of the bad weather in Buffalo, Butker made sure to acknowledge that wasn’t a viable excuse on a day where the opponent made two kicks from over 54 yards. “No,” Butker responded. “Obviously, Tyler Bass did a great job handling it, and you have to make the kicks.” Earlier in the game, Butker hit a 26-yard field goal. He also made an extra point. He felt the difference between the misses and makes. “The one I made felt good,” Butker said. “It hit higher up on my foot. The miss, it was just toey and I pushed it off to the right.” “I can’t explain it,” Butker finished. “I’m missing kicks and you don’t want that to happen.” Butker wasn’t the only Chiefs special teams player to have a blunder in Buffalo. The latest game filled with mistakes from the third phase prompted Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star to ask Andy Reid about the special teams leadership after the game. “We have to do better,” Reid said. “But the leadership, I feel comfortable with.” While Butker may have to look over his shoulder at a potential practice-squad elevation in the future, special teams coordinator Dave Toub seems to be just fine with the head coach.

title: Cowboys’ Brian Schottenheimer Breaks Silence on Calls for His Firing
summary: The Dallas Cowboys had a 31-10 lead over the Philadelphia Eagles late in the third quarter on Thanksgiving. They still found a way to lose. content: Fans want Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer fired after Thursday's loss to the Eagles Getty Head coach Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys looks on during the game against the San Francisco 49ers at AT&T Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) Getty The pressure is on Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer Getty The Dallas Cowboys had a 31-10 lead over the Philadelphia Eagles late in the third quarter on Thanksgiving. They still found a way to lose. The Eagles stormed back for a 39-38 win — the largest Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history. That dropped Dallas to 5-7 and put its playoff hopes on life support. It also has Cowboys fans demanding that head coach Brian Schottenheimer be fired — some of them before he even got home for Thanksgiving dinner. Brian Schottenheimer’s Job Security Suddenly a Hot Topic Getty Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer is firmly not he hot seat after losing to the Eagles When he was asked about his job security after the game, the second-year head coach kept it short despite the growing pressure from fans for owner Jerry Jones to make a coaching change. “I don’t worry about that,” Schottenheimer said, per The Athletic’s Jon Machota. “I worry about the guys in that locker room. That doesn’t affect me.” He did admit he was “very disappointed,” and he made it clear he isn’t going anywhere on his own. “I’m disappointed in the outcome of this game,” Schottenheimer said. “I’m disappointed in the fact that we’re 5-7. I’m a worker. That’s what I do. The grit and the fight with those guys in that locker room, I believe in it. I believe it’s real. So, I’m gonna stand with them shoulder to shoulder.” That might not be enough to win over the fan base though. The biggest mistake of the night was arguably Schottenheimer’s. With a two-point lead and 55 seconds left, he went for it on fourth-and-1 from the Eagles’ 39-yard line instead of punting, and quarterback Dak Prescott was sacked. Philadelphia was out of timeouts at the time. A short punt could have pinned the Eagles deep in their own end. Instead, Joe Milton got them in range for Jake Elliott’s game-winning 60-yard field goal. For now, Schottenheimer still has the backing of his boss. Owner Jerry Jones told reporters that firing his coach is “certainly not the thought on my mind at this particular time.” “We’ve got several more games to go and we’ve got to have our mind on that,” Jones added. Cowboys Fans Want Brian Schottenheimer Gone Getty The pressure is on Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer Cowboys fans didn’t hold back with their frustration toward Schottenheimer. “If Jerry doesn’t fire Schottenheimer tonight, then he is not a serious owner,” one fan wrote. “Fire Schottenheimer. Fire CP. Fire Pettine. Fire everyone except Dak, Javonte, GP, CeeDee, and JPJ,” another fan commented. “FIRE BRIAN SCHOTTENHEIMER BEFORE HE GETS ANY THANKSGIVING DINNER,” one user posted. “We are witnessing one of the worst head coaches in Dallas Cowboys franchise history in Brian Schottenheimer,” remarked another. It’s easy to understand their frustration. The Cowboys went 7-9-1 in Schottenheimer’s first season, and Year 2 has been even rockier. Dallas blew a game to the Arizona Cardinals in a 33-30 overtime loss. Then it gave up 46 points in a 40-point effort against the San Francisco 49ers, which dropped the team to 4-6. After that loss, Schottenheimer took defensive play-calling duties away from first-year coordinator Christian Parker and handed them to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine. It didn’t matter on Thursday. The Cowboys gave up 29 points after the 31-10 lead, including 22 in the fourth quarter alone. Schottenheimer still has just one win streak since taking over as head coach last year. title: Cowboys vs. Eagles recap: Dallas embarrassed by Philadelphia on Thanksgiving Day
summary: The Cowboys are a national embarrassment
content: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 26: Ceedee Lamb #88 of the Dallas Cowboys is tackled by Andrew Mukuba #24 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the second quarter at AT&T Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images It will go down in history as one of the darkest Thanksgiving Day games ever for the Dallas Cowboys. Somehow, some way, the Cowboys threw away a 31-10 lead that they had in the third quarter. The Philadelphia Eagles won on what was basically a game-winning, 60-yard field goal. It is hard to fathom. On the other hand it is actually very easy to fathom given everything we have seen from the Cowboys this season. They are not a good football team. They are poorly coached. They are talent-deficient. They are all of the bad things. On a day where we are supposed to be thankful it is hard to find a reason to be for this specific part of our lives. The Dallas Cowboys are a weekly embarrassment and Thursday was the latest example of it. What even happens now? First Quarter The Eagles won the toss and deferred which put the Cowboys offense to work first. Dak Prescott and the group did not waste the opportunity. Javonte Williams was served seconds, thirds, and then some as the team marched down the field, partly thanks to a huge 3rd and 18 conversion from Dak to CeeDee Lamb, but it was Williams who capped it off with the touchdown to give the home team an early 7-0 lead. JAVONTE TD pic.twitter.com/IFq12RHEEy — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 Things were looking rather impressive for Joe Milton and the Eagles. I’d imagine that many Cowboys fans were starting to assume a score was happening any minute across the first drive. Thankfully that was not the case. Right around field goal range the Eagles chose to roll the dice on fourth and short… and Quinnen Williams said no! QUINNEN!!! pic.twitter.com/Yz2K1cZsqi — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 Weirdly a sequence occurred on the next drive that did the first. Dak Prescott scrambled for a first on a third down, but the gain was negated by a penalty. This brought up third and long (16 here, 18 before) and Prescott connected with a star receiver (George Pickens here, CeeDee Lamb before) for the first down. After that KaVontae Turpin had a stellar catch where he turned on the boosters and reached the endzone in a flash. Dallas was up 14-0 early. TURP TD!!!! pic.twitter.com/8ihtwLzjs2 — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 The quarter ended with Philly holding the ball right after. Second Quarter The Eagles punted shortly after teams flipped the field which put the Cowboys offense back up. Given that they were already leading 14-0 this was a chance to really blow things open. Unfortunately they could not and wound up punting the ball for the first time in a while. A big 3rd and 12 conversion from Philadelphia put them within striking distance and while they were unable to fully get home they did give Jake Elliott a chance at a 48-yard field goal. It was good and the visitors had their first points on the day. The Cowboys offense did not miss this time around. KaVontae Turpin was involved again, this time on a jet sweep, and there was a big conversion from Dak Prescott to CeeDee Lamb. But it was Javonte Williams who cased in yet again. This marked his second score on the day and gave Dallas a 21-3 lead. JAVONTE WILLIAMS AGAIN pic.twitter.com/mbe4qovd3I — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 The dam finally broke, though. Joe Milton had been showing moments of promise to this point in the game and at long last he delivered. It was a classic Joe Milton throw… meaning it traveled quite a long ways. JOE MILTON'S ARM TALENT IS RIDICULOUS 🎯 PHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/Tubi Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2MLAir7i29 — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 The Cowboys received the ball with just over four minutes to go. It felt like an important possession as it would likely be their last one before the half and they received the ball to start the game. Points were essential. In all honesty it was a pretty penalty-filled drive. Officials were calling them left and right, many of them helping the Cowboys, but Dallas was moved back after an apparent touchdown to Brevyn Spann-Ford. On third and goal from the 12-yard line… Dak Prescott found Javonte Williams for a score to close the half. It also marked a hat trick of scores on the day for Williams specifically. JAVONT3 pic.twitter.com/9lMQ1ebII8 — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) November 26, 2026 The Eagles took a knee and it was Miranda Lambert time. Third Quarter Philadelphia went three and out to start the second half which is always great to see. The Cowboys took the field and once again with an opportunity to stretch their lead. Dallas punted it back themselves. This game truly felt over, but obviously with a lot of time left that was not the case in any real way. Football had to be played. Shemar James sacked Joe Milton which helped to ensure the punt streak continued. Philly booted it back and the Cowboys offense returned to the field. It was a little bit of the same for the Cowboys offense in terms of not being able to fully convert. They did score, but only 3 points by way of Brandon Aubrey. This was notable though as it was a 59-yard field goal that he drilled with ease which was great to see given how this season has gone. The FOX broadcast also noted that this was the longest ever field goal made on Thanksgiving all-time. Pretty neat. The third quarter ended right as Philadelphia crossed the 50-yard line… and then Joe Milton found DeVonta Smith again to get another touchdown on the board with 15 seconds left. It was suddenly 31-17, good guys. Fourth Quarter Things did not go particularly well for the Cowboys offense to start the fourth quarter. They faced a fourth and short on their side of the field and left the offense on the field. It was bold, but nobody really thought they were going to run a play. Thankfully they just fished for offsides and punted. Or so we thought. The Cowboys tried to punt… but it was blocked and returned for a Philly touchdown. title: Eagles mount furious comeback, beat Cowboys 39-38 in Thanksgiving classic
summary: What looked like a blowout turned into a great one, as Philadelphia stormed back to win in Dallas.
content: It was a Thanksgiving Day classic in Dallas. In a wild game that went from an apparent blowout to a thrilling comeback, the Cowboys jumped out to a 31-10 lead and then lost 39-38 when Eagles kicker Jake Elliott hit a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left. Eagles quarterback Joe Milton played by far the best game of his career, throwing for 331 yards, with three touchdown passes and a touchdown run. We've always known Milton had a strong arm, but he showed today that he's more than just a thrower. He can lead an NFL offense as a quarterback. But Dak Prescott is a good quarterback, too, and he turned in a big game of his own. He threw for 291 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions. Prescott's favorite receiver was CeeDee Lamb, who finished with 134 receiving yards, and running back Javonte Williams ran for two touchdowns and also caught a touchdown pass. The Eagles, however, got a monster game from wide receiver DeVonta Smith, who had 11 catches for 200 yards and two touchdowns. Smith was sensational while the Eagles were coming back in the fourth quarter. Special teams miscues killed the Cowboys: The Eagles blocked a punt for a touchdown, and Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal in the fourth quarter. Aubrey, who became the highest-paid kicker in the NFL this offseason, is having the worst season of his career. The loss drops the Cowboys to 5-7 and is devastating to their playoff hopes. The 4-7 Eagles aren't contenders, but they played like contenders today.

title: ‘That was freaking insane’: Chicago Bears stay ‘super resilient’ to rally and pull off a 39-35 win
summary: When Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze toe-tapped in the end zone for a 6-yard go-ahead touchdown catch with 3 seconds left Thursday, it transported Sam Roush back to the frenzied fourth-quarter rallies of last season — and the rookie tight end wasn’t even on the team then. “I remember being in college (at Stanford) watching (the Bears) last year and being like, ‘How is this even ...
content: When Chicago Bears wide receiver Rome Odunze toe-tapped in the end zone for a 6-yard go-ahead touchdown catch with 3 seconds left Thursday, it transported Sam Roush back to the frenzied fourth-quarter rallies of last season — and the rookie tight end wasn’t even on the team then. “I remember being in college (at Stanford) watching (the Bears) last year and being like, ‘How is this even possible?’” he said after the Bears’ 39-35 comeback thriller over the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving Day at Ford Field. “And now I get to be a part of it.” Odunze’s score was the first time the Bears led all game. “Obviously, I’m not the guy that made those big plays today, but seeing Rome do that was incredible at the end of the game,” Roush said. “And (quarterback) Caleb (Williams), like, that’s why they call Caleb ‘Ice Man.’ Like, that was freaking insane. “We just got some dogs in the game.” If there’s a word that describes the Bears on Thursday, it’s “dogged.” There were several points in the game that looked like backbreakers, and some of the setbacks that seemed almost insurmountable. • Midway through the first quarter, tight end Colston Loveland lost a fumble after his only catch. • Later in the first, the Bears lost Loveland for the rest of the game after he injured his knee while blocking on a run play. • The Bears’ chance to mount a 2-minute drill before halftime ended with Williams taking a strip-sack and a safety. • When Jahmyr Gibbs sprinted 70 yards for a fourth-quarter touchdown, it looked like a wrap. Bears running back D’Andre Swift said they remained unfazed, even as the Lions built an 11-point advantage after Gibbs’s scamper pushed Detroit’s lead to 35-24 with 8 minutes, 20 seconds left in the game. “We (were) always in the game, and I feel like the game never really got away from us,” Swift said. “We gave up some stuff early on and kind of made it hard for us. “But it was a heavyweight fight. Back and forth, back and forth. Went down to the wire.” Swift had a 30-yard touchdown run, and Kyle Monangai ran in 1- and 2-yard touchdowns, scores that helped keep the Bears engaged in a seesaw battle in the second and third quarters. Odunze’s two touchdown receptions both came in the fourth quarter. The Bears defense coughed up 205 rushing yards and three touchdowns to Gibbs, but also came up with a pair of crucial plays. “Defense came up in critical situations,” Swift said. “It’s how we fight as a team. “That’s the one word I would use for that win is just ‘fight.’” Rookie safety Dillon Thieneman caught his third interception of the season (and second in consecutive games) after Jared Goff’s fourth-quarter pass bounced off receiver Jameson Williams’ hands and into Thieneman’s chest. The offense couldn’t convert that pick into points, but it didn’t stall a Lions drive that reached the Chicago 34-yard line and likely cost Detroit at least a field goal try. “I felt like that was a big change, and then giving it to the offense and all them to build some more momentum with that,” Thieneman said. “I felt it was really important.” On another crucial defensive play, T.J. Edwards wrangled Gibbs to the ground after a 1-yard catch on fourth-and-4, where nothing was backing up Edwards but a lot of green turf. Edwards’ stop forced the Lions to turn the ball over on downs. The offense then marched 68 yards on 13 plays in 2 minutes, 14 seconds, with Odunze’s toe-drag touchdown capping it off. Like Roush, Thieneman isn’t used to these kinds of wild finishes. “It’s awesome, he said. “Definitely a lot of ups and downs. You gotta control yourself, gotta stay level in it all.” Throughout the game, various players and coaches would make uplifting comments such as “don’t forget we’ve got a game to win, we’re still in this,” Kalif Raymond said. “I remember, I want to say, (quarterbacks coach) J.T. Barrett came out on the sidelines, like, ‘Hey, man, we’re in this. This game is down to the wire.’” Last season, the Bears engineered seven late-game comebacks between the regular season and playoffs. This season, they’ve taken more leads and spent more time fending off comebacks, so Thursday’s game was the first true nailbiter. “Man, I’m really proud of our guys,” Ben Johnson said. “I think about how far we’ve come since we’ve been in the building the last year and a half. Just the professionalism with which they conduct themselves, the hard work they put in all season long, but certainly on a short week like this. “And then the belief that they had in a game like that, particularly when we gave them some momentum at halftime. And yet to be able to weather that storm.” Linebacker D’Marco Jackson said the team had heard the chatter about the Bears’ struggles in the NFC North (2-6 under Johnson heading into the matchup), so to steal a win on the road against a division opponent, under those circumstances, was “super huge.” “I think a lot of people wrote us off thinking we weren’t going to be able to come in here and pull it off,” Jackson said. “We did just that and we put everybody on notice.” Roush also learned about the makeup of the team. “Super resilient,” he said. “Lot of playmakers. … It really is incredible. We’re still hungry.”

title: Instant analysis: What went right, what went wrong in the Bills' win over the Chiefs
summary: An analysis of Buffalo's performance vs. the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 12.
content: The Buffalo Bills outlasted the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10 in a waterlogged, defensive-minded affair. Tyler Bass made a 57-yard field to give the Bills the victory as time exprired. The weather completely impacted this game, neutralizing the Bills aerial attack. Buffalo's offense could only total 81yards through the air. James Cook became the focal point for the Bills offense, earning 33 touches on the evening. Cook scored the Bills only touchdown in the game. Buffalo's defense did enough to keep the Chiefs offense from gaining consistent momentum. Kansas City moved the ball fairly well in the conditions. However, the Bills defense held the Chiefs to only one touchdown. Here is an instant analysis of what went right in the Bills victory over the Chiefs. What went right? James Cook: Cook rushed the ball 32 times for 117 yards and a touchdown. Buffalo's passing attack was nonexistent, so the ground game picked up the slack. Cook fought hard for yards, often grabbing an extra yard or two per rush to give Buffalo better field position. Special teams: Tyler Bass was the star in the fourth quarter. Bass hammered two long field goals in the fourth quarter, including the game-winning 57-yard field goal in the substandard conditions. Tommy Doman pinned the Chiefs deep in their territory multiple times and averaged over 45 yards per punt (even after one shanked punt that only traveled 25 yards). On the final Kansas City punt, upback Joe Andreessen appeared to tip the punt. Greg Dortch returned the punt 17 yards to put the Bills in field goal range for the win. Greg Rousseau: Rousseau was a menace once again, registering four tackles, a sack, and three quarterback hits. Buffalo's defense: The Bills defense kept the Chiefs from hitting any big plays. The unit locked down the Chiefs offense, forcing multiple field goal attempts when Kansas City entered scoring range. In addition, the Bills defense forced seven punts during the night. The Chiefs converted only two-of-eleven third-down attempts. What went wrong? The passing attack: It didn't exist in the game. Josh Allen did not look comfortable passing the ball in the game. The conditions limited his accuracy all evening. Allen completed only 10-of-21 passes for 81 yards. In addition, Allen threw two interceptions in the red zone, which is not ideal in a game where points are at a premium. Second-half struggles: The Chiefs scored quickly on the first drive of the second half. Kansas City completed a seven-play, 56-yard drive in three-and-a-half minutes, culminating with an Emmett Johnson touchdown. Buffalo's offense started the half with two 12-play drives. However, the first ended with a turnover, while the second stalled out and finished with a field goal. The bottom line Buffalo won its seventh consecutive game. The victory keeps the Bills at the top of the AFC playoff standings. The win also gives the Bills an advantage if a tie-breaking scenario occurs with the Chiefs, as the Bills have the head-to-head advantage. It's a big win for the Bills, as the team did it without the best, or even adequate play, from their MVP candidate. Josh Allen struggled mightily, so Buffalo became a one-dimensional offensive attack. Cook carried the load, and the offensive line won the battle in the trenches. Buffalo's defense was solid. The Chiefs had moments where their offense looked good. However, Buffalo's defense shut things down when they needed it the most. It's promising that the unit can keep the game in check, espeically when the offense is not producing points. What's next? Buffalo travels to Foxborough to take on the New England Patriots on December 6. Buffalo's loss to New England in Week 5 is the Bills only blemish on their record this year. New England lost its previous two games leading into Week 12. The Patriots have struggled since the loss of Drake Maye due to a long-term injury. New England squares off against the Los Angeles Chargers this Sunday. title: The J.J. McCarthy improvement that could get Giants to the next level
summary: The deep balls were flying from the right arm of J.J. McCarthy, but the connections were tough to come by.
content: New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) passes over Jacksonville Jaguars defensive end Travon Walker (44) in East Rutherford, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. The deep balls were flying from the right arm of J.J. McCarthy, but the connections were tough to come by. Deep to rookie Malachi Fields, incomplete. Access the Giants like never before Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers. tRY IT NOW Deep to Malik Nabers, incomplete. Deep to Darnell Mooney, incomplete. Another one deep to Fields, interception overturned upon review to an incomplete pass. Deep to Mooney over the middle, incomplete. Yet another deep shot to Mooney on third-and-17, not close, and some boos ensued from the crowd at MetLife Stadium. “At the end of the day, I just missed them,” McCarthy said. “The big thing that kind of stood out to me was just put some more air on the ball and let the receivers be able to track it a little bit better, but that’s an easy fix and we’ll get it fixed.” These down-the-field attempts from McCarthy were part of his 20 incomplete passes in the 23-18 upset victory over the Jaguars, showing that the Giants have to be really good, but not perfect, to beat a quality opponent. McCarthy has been a godsend since arriving in a trade with the Vikings — that 2027 fifth-round pick was draft capital well spent — and he takes a 3-1 record as the Giants starting quarterback into Sunday’s game with the Colts in Indianapolis. Ever since his arrival Sept. 29, it has been a full-speed-ahead crash course for McCarthy, as far as learning a brand-new offense and trying to fast-forward his comfort with the unfamiliar players around him. Building chemistry with wide receivers and tight ends takes time, and that was not on McCarthy’s side. The reputation for having a strong arm and a nice feel for the deep ball preceded McCarthy to his second NFL stop. That is the next bit of firepower to add to his arsenal as the Giants look to secure and build on their first-place lead in the NFC East. New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) passes over Jacksonville Jaguars defensive end Travon Walker (44) in East Rutherford, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Adam Hunger “For me, personally, just having more time on task with my guys being able to hit the ones that are there, especially the deeper shots,” McCarthy said. “Just being able to get in here and work with the guys just constantly and just be able to get those reps over and over again. “But I’m going to make those. Those are things that are going to come and have shown up, but sometimes you just miss. In this league, you can’t miss too many times. So just being able to be ready for that next opportunity and nail it.” McCarthy has not pushed the ball into the end zone as often as the Giants would like. He has only two touchdown passes in his four starts. Some of this is happenstance — the Giants had four rushing touchdowns in McCarthy’s first start, a 27-21 overtime victory in Houston. Some of this is McCarthy at times still looking a bit uncertain within the offense, as far as going through his progressions. Making the timely throw, and finding a way to win, though, are McCarthy hallmarks. That is how he went 27-1 at Michigan. His stats were often mid-level — the Wolverines were largely a running team during his time in Ann Arbor — but when a throw or a run was needed to keep a drive alive, McCarthy delivered with impressive regularity. New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy (18) speaks at a press conference in East Rutherford, N.J., Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. Robert Sabo for NY Post McCarthy was spraying the ball down the stretch against the Jaguars as the Giants fell into a second-half rut, with four consecutive possessions failing to pick up a first down. When it came time to close out the game or else hand it back over to Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars offense, McCarthy came through with his most clutch throw. He wanted to find Nabers on the left side, but Nabers was shadowed by two defenders. No opening there. McCarthy instantly pivoted and fired a strike to Fields for a 19-yard completion. That alleviated a great deal of pressure. After two 5-yard runs from Cam Skattebo, McCarthy could kneel down three times to end it. “That was my second read,’’ McCarthy said of the pass to Fields. “There are so many things that you could really look at from your perspective and everyone has — they’re entitled to their own perspective and their own opinion, but if you’re not really in the room and you don’t understand what the progressions are. Sometimes it’s zone-based or man-based coverage reads where it’s like, yeah, it might be your first progression, but it’s really the second in your thought process of what the defense has given you. It’s little things like that where you just can’t really focus on and just got to worry about doing your job as a quarterback, which is throwing to the open guy, and sometimes, a lot of the times, with good defenses, that is going through your reads.” And, sometimes, those reads lead to deep throws down the field. “Come back and make the next throw, and that’s a confident guy, and he’s been in a lot of huge games,” coach John Harbaugh said. “And we’re going to start hitting some of those deep passes. We wanted to take some shots, we wanted to go after them downfield and we did, and those are going to start happening. We’ll start making those plays for sure.”

title: Is there an NFL game today? Which teams play on Black Friday?

content: Black Friday isn't just a day for shopping around for the best deals. It's now also a day for football . In case three NFL games on Thanksgiving weren't enough, the league is hosting its fourth-ever Black Friday game. The NFL held its first Black Friday game in 2023. While Thanksgiving is most commonly associated with football, the NFL turned it into a full weekend experience as the Denver Broncos and Pittsburgh Steelers face off a day after America consumed copious amounts of turkey. Here's what you need to know about the NFL Black Friday game, including how to tune in. Which NFL teams play on Black Friday? The Denver Broncos will travel to Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, to face the Steelers on Black Friday. Both the Steelers and Broncos made the playoffs in 2025 but suffered tough losses that kept them shy of a Super Bowl appearance. This Week 12 game between the two teams could play a significant part in determining the AFC playoff picture in 2026. What time does the Broncos vs. Steelers game start? 3 p.m. ET. Kickoff for the NFL's Black Friday game is scheduled for 3 p.m. ET. It is the lone game of the day and fits in just before the typical late slate of games football fans enjoy on Sundays. Because Amazon Prime Video is not carrying any of the Thursday games, which it typically does during the regular season, the streaming-only network is carrying the NFL's Black Friday game. Local viewers in Denver and Pittsburgh can catch the game on cable. Al Michaels will be on the call with analyst Kirk Herbstreit and sideline reporter Kaylee Hartung.
