title: NFL Under Fire After Refs’ Controversial Call Wipes Out Eagles TD Following Javonte Williams Fumble During Cowboys Clash
summary: An officiating decision in the Eagles-Cowboys game has put the NFL’s review process under scrutiny again. Philadelphia’s touchdown, which came after a Javonte Williams fumble, was taken off the board by the officials, and the play never counted.
content: LANDOVER, MD – DECEMBER 25: Dallas Cowboys running back Javonte Williams 33 reads his blockers during game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Washington Commanders on December 25, 2025 at Northwest Stadium in Landover, MD. Photo by Charles Brock/Icon Sportswire NFL, American Football Herren, USA DEC 25 Cowboys at Commanders EDITORIAL USE ONLY Icon251225004 ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire An officiating decision in the Eagles-Cowboys game has put the NFL’s review process under scrutiny again. Philadelphia’s touchdown, which came after a Javonte Williams fumble, was taken off the board by the officials, and the play never counted. The officials’ interpretation of forward progress is disputed; some analysts argue Williams did fumble before being ruled down. Nevertheless, the ruling has now prompted fans and analysts to question how the rule was applied and whether the league enforces it consistently across games. “Whistle halts Riq Woolen return after Javonte Williams fumble. Nick Sirianni protested the early stoppage,” Wire Report NFL posted on X . Williams was driving toward the end zone when the ball came loose just short of the goal line in the second quarter. Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen scooped it up and took off for a 97-yard return that looked like a touchdown. Before he got there, the whistle blew. The officials ruled that Williams’ forward progress had already been stopped, which meant the play was dead before Woolen reached the end zone, preventing a TD rather than erasing one. When a touchdown gets erased in a rivalry game, the entire playoff picture shifts. Stay ahead of every controversial call and its impact with EssentiallySports NFL coverage. That ruling carries a harsh consequence, because forward progress calls can’t be challenged. Nick Sirianni had nothing to throw a flag over and no review to ask for, so the Eagles simply had to line up again. Dallas then scored its own touchdown to build the halftime cushion. By the start of the fourth quarter, the Cowboys led 31-17, with Philadelphia having added ten points in the second quarter and seven in the third. The officials’ call on it is now drawing heavy criticism. One fan, whose comment was originally in Spanish, summed up how it looked from the stands: “To me, this was a fumble by Javonte Williams and a potential defensive TD for the Eagles that would have made it 21-17 at halftime. The refs blew the whistle (too early, in my opinion), and that killed the play. Anyway… on to the next one.” Media voices were just as direct. Former ESPN writer Ed Werder pointed to how plays like this are usually handled: “That was a quick whistle on the potential Javonte Williams fumble and Eagles recovery. They usually allow that to play out through the return. Riq Woolen was stopped from a 98-yard return by whistle. Nick Sirianni had a legit argument and made it.” Eagles reporter Brandon Lee Gowton was far less diplomatic, as he said on X, “Absolute horseshit ruling on that Javonte Williams fumble creates a 14-point swing in the Cowboys’ favor. Abysmal officiating.” Interestingly, the frustration wasn’t limited to Philadelphia’s side. Cowboys beat reporter Joseph Hoyt saw it the same way. “They’re going to say his forward progress is stopped, but Javonte Williams did fumble that, it was a clear recovery, and Tariq Woolen took it back for a TD. Cowboys catch a HUGE break,” Hoyt wrote on X. Fan comments piled up too. One take captured the mood of the Eagles faithful. “Eagles fans feel robbed 😤 Philly appeared to rip the ball from Javonte Williams near the goal line, but officials ruled his forward progress was stopped, and the call wasn’t reviewable. #FlyEaglesFly” And one fan directed his anger straight at the league’s officiating account. :@NFLOfficiating enough of this garbage of a product you have out there. Fine them, fire them, do something!”, a fan wrote. A call that can’t be reviewed leaves nothing but the debate, and this one will be argued for a long time. title: Pat McAfee Comes to Brandon Aubrey’s Defense & Blames Cowboys Snapper for Missed Field Goal
summary: The Dallas Cowboys’ Thanksgiving game did not go as planned, despite making significant headway in the first two quarters of the game. But the Philadelphia Eagles made a late-game comeback, scoring 22 points in the final quarter itself.
content: November 15, 2025, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA: November 15, 2025: Pat McAfee on ESPN College Game Day during the University of Pittsburgh Panthers vs. Notre Dame Fighting Irish at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh PA. Brook Ward / Apparent Media Group Pittsburgh USA – ZUMAa234 20251115_zsa_a234_326 Copyright: xAMGx ©IMAGO/ZUMA Press Wire The Dallas Cowboys’ Thanksgiving game did not go as planned, despite making significant headway in the first two quarters of the game. But the Philadelphia Eagles made a late-game comeback, scoring 22 points in the final quarter itself. What sealed their narrow 39-38 win over the Cowboys was a missed field goal opportunity by Brandon Aubrey, earning the Cowboys kicker a fair amount of criticism. But NFL analyst Pat McAfee pushed back against the Brandon Aubrey slander with an X post uploaded on November 26 , pointing out the real reason Aubrey missed. “Just a reminder.. In modern football, [with] long snapping being a full time job, the snapper is 90% responsible for the laces,” McAfee wrote. The opportunity for the field goal came late in the fourth quarter with three minutes and 27 seconds left on the clock. On fourth-and-5 play at Philadelphia’s 22-yard line, holder Bryan Anger placed the ball but failed to turn the laces around in time before Aubrey kicked the ball. With the Cowboys kicker making contact with the side of the ball with the laces out, the 40-yard attempt flew wide left rather than straight through the uprights. When a kicker takes heat, the details matter. Subscribe to stay across the Cowboys' roster drama and the technical breakdowns reshaping playoff narratives. The miss proved to be disastrous for the Cowboys and prevented them from establishing an 11-point lead that would have sealed their win. But the Eagles soon scored a touchdown and a field goal that gave them a single-point lead with two seconds left on the clock. But while most critics blamed Aubrey for costing the Cowboys their sixth win of the season, McAfee pointed out that there was a reason why the NFL had stepped away from the tradition of using backup centers or punters as long snappers. He reasoned that the entire responsibility of a long snapper was to perfectly snap the ball to the punter or the holder, who spotted it on the ground just before the kicker struck it. So, the responsibility of making sure that the laces were not facing the kicker fell on the snapper, rather than the holder or the kicker. In the NFL, a long snapper controls where the laces land by repeating the exact same snap tempo, grip, and distance every time, which allows the ball to complete a certain number of rotations before reaching the holder. In this case, McAfee assigned the blame to the Cowboys’ long snapper Trent Sieg. He believed that Sieg was the one who should have been held accountable for his role, which was to make sure the ball landed with the laces facing away from Aubrey when he made the field goal attempt. During the postgame conference, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer also addressed the missed opportunity. Rather than blaming Aubrey, the head coach stated that he was going to reserve his judgment until he watched the film and assessed the special team’s overall execution. title: Recent opponents reportedly spill truth about Patriots 'soft' defense
summary: The Patriots' defense was reportedly called "soft" by recent opponents.
content: The perception from some of the New England Patriots' recent opponents is that the defensive unit is "soft." That's a major turnaround for a unit that was considered one of the best in the NFL last season. With that said, the Patriots have given up 99 points in total over the last three games. That includes 35 points against the Detroit Lions and 45 points against the Green Bay Packers. There really is no sugar-coating the fact that it has looked like a disaster at times against top-tier offensive teams. Even worse, those other teams are starting to talk about it. "I've had conversations with people that have played the Patriots of late, and that is a word that has come up about their defense is soft," Perry said on Zolak & Bertrand . "And softer than what they were anticipating I think, too, because you have some big names, especially up front there like in the interior and the way they were moved in that Lions game I think surprised a lot of people." The defensive front has struggled to stop the run and get home consistently enough to impact opposing quarterbacks. However, one of the more disappointing problems for the Patriots has been their defensive backfield. Star cornerback Christian Gonzalez hasn't played up to his potential, and Carlton Davis Davis hasn't been available due to injury. Kevin Byard has also struggled at safety. There is also the fact that defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr hasn't been as effective as a play-caller as he was a year ago. Overall, it has been a frustrating season for a defensive unit that came into the year with high expectations. The good news is that there is still time left to turn things around with the hardest stretch of football still ahead. Follow Patriots Wire on Twitter and Facebook . title: ‘He’s a Strange Guy,’ ‘The One Thing You Don’t Do’ — Steelers Legend Terry Bradshaw Doesn’t Mince Words About Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy Drama
summary: Pittsburgh Steelers legend Terry Bradshaw picked a side in the Aaron Rodgers saga, and it was Mike McCarthy’s. Bradshaw minced no words on FOX’s Thanksgiving pregame show on Thursday.
content: Mike McCarthy, Aaron Rodgers and Terry Bradshaw Pittsburgh Steelers legend Terry Bradshaw picked a side in the Aaron Rodgers saga, and it was Mike McCarthy’s. Bradshaw minced no words on FOX’s Thanksgiving pregame show on Thursday. He stood with McCarthy, the head coach, and the Rooney family a day after the Steelers released Rodgers, who had leveled a string of accusations at McCarthy on “The Pat McAfee Show.” Terry Bradshaw Faults the Way Aaron Rodgers Left Pittsburgh Bradshaw began with the Rooneys and McCarthy, and he was open about his own ties: “Growing up in that family, the Rooney family especially, I would say this: they’re a classy, classy bunch, classy organization. Mike McCarthy and I have been friends for years. Classy man. I don’t know all the details. … I’m sorry that Aaron Rodgers had to do this. … Am I surprised? Absolutely not. To my opinion, he’s a strange guy anyway.” Notably, the heart of his criticism was how Rodgers went about leaving: “And the one thing you don’t do—all of us athletes up here, including you, none of us turn on our teammates. We don’t turn on our coaching staff. We don’t turn on our ownership. We show class on the way out. Aaron Rodgers didn’t do that.” He also turned to something he remembered Rodgers saying about life after Pittsburgh: “And one thing I’m reminded of. He said, when my—when I’m through playing here in Pittsburgh, I’ll disappear and you’ll never hear or see from me again. And I hope this is one time he’s telling the truth.” Bradshaw was reacting to a whirlwind few days in Pittsburgh. The Steelers benched Rodgers for Mason Rudolph on Tuesday night, ahead of Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos. On Wednesday, Rodgers went on McAfee’s show and accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings and skipping others, along with team events. Rodgers was indeed blunt about where he stood on the benching and the play-calling: “If you try and bench me or don’t change the play-calling, then you should just release me, because I feel like, at this point, I’m doing what’s right for the organization.” RUN YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Ultimate GM Simulator McCarthy, who made the call to bench Rodgers, met reporters later Wednesday and kept the details to himself, though he called what Rodgers had made an “ultimatum.” Incidentally, the Steelers cut Rodgers the same day. Meanwhile, team president Art Rooney II made the organization’s position clear on Thursday in an interview with the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac: “I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond. The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.” Rooney also pointed to the teammates Rodgers left behind: “There’s maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload. … He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don’t do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that’s for sure.” When asked whether he regretted signing Rodgers, Rooney said: “I’m disappointed the way it came out. … But we had a good experience last year, and so I kind of wasn’t expecting it to go this way this year.” Rodgers and McCarthy go back a long way. They spent 13 years together in Green Bay, including a Super Bowl XLV win over Pittsburgh, and the Steelers turned to McCarthy after 19 seasons under Mike Tomlin. Rodgers returned this past spring for a second season in Pittsburgh on a one-year contract with $22 million guaranteed. The 42-year-old QB cleared waivers Thursday and is now a free agent. He is 29th in PFN’s QB Impact Rankings with a grade of 67.2. Rodgers has said 2026 will be his final NFL season, though he has not said whether he intends to sign with another team for the remainder of it. title: Stunner! Eagles rally from 21 down to beat Cowboys 39-38. 4 takeaways
summary: The Eagles rallied from 21 points down late in the third quarter to beat the Dallas Cowboys 39-38
content: ARLINGTON, Texas − It took 10 games, but finally, the Eagles ' offense had by far the output of the season, with quarterback Joe Milton throwing two long touchdown passes to DeVonta Smith, one for 50 yards and the other for 45. The Eagles also blocked a punt and recovered the ball for a touchdown. They needed all of it, including a 60-yard field goal by Jake Elliott with 2 seconds left as they rallied from 21 points down late in the third quarter to stun the Dallas Cowboys 39-38 on Nov. 26. Buy Philadelphia Eagles tickets The Eagles had scored their most points in any game this season, by far, as embattled offensive coordinator Sean Mannion and the offense finally showed its potential. And that was with running back Saquon Barkley and tight end Dallas Goedert leaving in the first quarter with injuries. The Eagles fell behind 21-3 midway through the second quarter, and 31-10 with 3:35 left late in the third quarter. That's when the Eagles finally got the offense going, or at least figured out that their best play was simply to throw the ball deep to Smith. The Eagles' star wide receiver finished with a career-high 200 yards receiving on 11 catches, to go along with two touchdowns. Milton, making only his third career start, went 21-for-31 for 331 yards with 3 TDs and an interception. Milton and Smith's first connection came with 4:06 left in the first half with the Eagles at midfield. Milton rolled to his left, motioned to Smith to keep going, and then fired the ball across the field and all the way into the end zone for a 50-yard touchdown. NextGen stats measured Milton's throw at 64.4 air yards. The two hooked up again for a 45-yarder with 15 seconds left in the third quarter. That pulled the Eagles to within 31-17. They were down by just seven points when Ty Robinson blocked Bryan Anger's punt as Kenny Moore scooped it up and ran it back three yards for a touchdown. The Eagles were within a touchdown for the first time since they fell behind 7-0 on the Cowboys' opening drive. But the Cowboys came right back on Prescott's 19-yard run. Milton answered with a 15-yard TD of his own to make it 38-30 with 9:09 left after the Eagles went for the two-point conversion and failed. But the Eagles got a break when Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal with 3:23 left. The Eagles went right to work as Milton hit Makai Lemon from 24 yards out. Again, the two-point conversion failed. But the Eagles had one more chance after they stopped the Cowboys on fourth down on Ty Robinson's sack with 50 seconds left. Then the Eagles barely got close enough for Elliott's 60-yard field goal, the second longest of his career. Here are three more takeaways: Joe Milton has a memorable game It was just Milton's third career start. But the Eagles' quarterback, a member of the Cowboys practice squad before the Eagles signed him on Oct. 16, made things happen with his arm (two long TDs) and his legs (a 15-yard TD run). In all, Milton was 21 of 31 for 331 yards and 3 touchdowns. Was it a fumble that could've turned game around? It appeared that Cowboys running back Javonte Williams fumbled the ball at the goal line late in the first half. On 1st-and-goal from the 1, Williams was stopped by Eagles defensive tackle Ty Robinson and the ball came out. Riq Woolen recovered the ball and was running towards the Cowboys end zone. But the play was blown dead as the officials said Williams' forward progress was stopped. Had it been ruled a fumble, and an Eagles touchdown, the Eagles would have cut the Cowboys' lead to 21-17. Instead, the Cowboys kept possession and scored with 4 seconds left in the half for a 28-10 lead. Rough game for Quinyon Mitchell Cornerback Quinyon Mitchell had his hands full against Cowboys receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. And that was before Cooper DeJean left early in the game with a concussion. Mitchell was called for three defensive penalties in the first half alone − two defensive pass interference calls and an illegal contact call. The second pass interference call was on Prescott's pass to CeeDee Lamb into the end zone, thus giving the Cowboys a first down at the Eagles' 1 yard line with less than a minute left in the first half. The Cowboys scored with 4 seconds left in the first half for a 28-10 lead. It wasn't just Mitchell, who was selected to the Pro Bowl in each of the last two seasons. Riq Woolen also had a tough time covering the Cowboys receivers. Woolen was beaten for a 36-yard completion to Pickens in the first quarter that set up the Cowboys' second touchdown. title: Terry Bradshaw calls Aaron Rodgers 'strange' and hopes he goes away

content: Terry Bradshaw called the Pittsburgh Steelers a classy organization Thursday evening. The Steelers Hall of Famer had much harsher words for Aaron Rodgers. "Am I surprised? Absolutely not. In my opinion, he's a strange guy anyway," the NFL analyst said during Fox's Thanksgiving pregame show. Bradshaw, who won four Super Bowls as the Steelers' quarterback from 1970 to 1983, also brought up Rodgers' vow to disappear once he is done playing. "And I hope this is one time he is telling the truth," Bradshaw said. Rodgers gave Bradshaw plenty of reason for the spicy comments. A day earlier, after the Steelers benched him for Mason Rudolph, Rodgers went on "The Pat McAfee Show," accused coach Mike McCarthy of sleeping through team meetings and said he wasn't coming back. The Steelers waived him that afternoon. Bradshaw said he has been friends with McCarthy for years and didn't know all the details, but he knew enough. "None of us turn on our teammates," Bradshaw said to the panel of former players with whom he co-hosts. "We don't turn on our coaching. We don't turn on our ownership. We show class on the way out. "Aaron Rodgers didn't do that." Bradshaw had never wanted Rodgers in Pittsburgh. In May 2025, while the Steelers were courting Rodgers, Bradshaw told 103.7 The Buzz in Arkansas that the quarterback should stay in California and "chew on bark." Rodgers, 43, laughed it off at the time. Now, the Steelers continue their season with Rudolph at quarterback , starting with the Black Friday game against the Broncos . Rodgers' future is up in the air. He's already said on McAfee's show that he's not going to be calling teams searching for new opportunities. "When this is done, it's Keyser Soze," Rodgers said. title: ‘Tom Brady Is Disgusted With Aaron Rodgers’ — NFL World Reacts As Legendary QB Makes Feelings Clear on Steelers-Mike McCarthy Controversy
summary: During Thursday’s Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys broadcast on FOX, Tom Brady addressed the messy split between Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers. He kept his tone calm and measured, but his message landed hard with many viewers.
content: ‘Tom Brady Is Disgusted With Aaron Rodgers’ — NFL World Reacts As Legendary QB Makes Feelings Clear on Steelers-Mike McCarthy Controversy During Thursday’s Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys broadcast on FOX, Tom Brady addressed the messy split between Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers. He kept his tone calm and measured, but his message landed hard with many viewers. The NFL legend and FOX analyst built his comments around what he called the sanctity of the locker room, and he said private matters should not be made public. Many fans and analysts heard that as a pointed rebuke of Rodgers. Reactions online came quickly, and several people said Brady had all but called Rodgers a bad teammate. Tom Brady Defends Sacred NFL Locker Room After Steelers Cut Aaron Rodgers The Steelers cut Rodgers, their starting quarterback and a four-time NFL MVP, after he went on Pat McAfee’s show on Wednesday and “basically burned the house down,” as Brady put it, criticizing Mike McCarthy and the whole organization. “It was a weird situation,” Brady said. He noted that the Steelers have a game on Friday and said they all now have to deal with the aftermath. For Brady, that was the core of the problem. The damage, in his view, does not stay with one player. It spills onto everyone else in the room. Brady then made the point he clearly wanted viewers to hear. He said an NFL locker room is “a very sacred place,” adding that “we shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players.” “It’s a privilege to be in that locker room, you’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together,” he said, adding that the locker room should not be the place for “private things to become public, that’s what I’ll say.” BUILD YOUR TEAM’S DRAFT: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator Brady did not dismiss what Rodgers has done on the field. He called Rodgers a Hall of Famer and said he is “a tremendous player.” He also said his criticism had “nothing to do with his play style.” Then came one of the more striking lines of the segment. “If that’s the last pass he throws, that’s a really sad way to end,” Brady said. From there, Brady drew on his own career. He said he was fortunate to be around a lot of great teammates over the years. “What made a great teammate to me was you cared about your teammates and your coaches and you cared about what the team was trying to accomplish,” he said. A moment later, he added: “And that supersedes any individual aspect of your game that you wanna promote.” PICK THE PLAYOFF FIELD: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Brady said again that he was fortunate to be in a great locker room. “I played for my teammates, I played for my coaches,” he said. He then closed with a line that summed up his view of the whole situation: “nobody wins when the family feuds.” Fans and Analysts React to Brady Burying Rodgers With Polite Criticism Brady never directly called Rodgers selfish or a bad teammate. Still, people read between the lines. Robin Lundberg, a WNBA analyst, put it bluntly in a post on X: “Tom Brady is disgusted with Aaron Rodgers.” Many fans read the comments the same way. They saw Brady choosing his words carefully while still making his feelings plain. One fan wrote that Brady “is doing everything he can right now to not call Rodgers a selfish loser. Basically said it as politely as possible.” Sports announcer Chase Snyder made a similar point about how far Brady went without saying the words outright, noting that “Tom Brady just said Aaron Rodgers is a bad teammate in every way he possibly could without directly saying he’s a bad teammate.” Jarrett Bailey, an NFL analyst, focused on the contrast between Brady’s tone and the weight of what he said. “Tom Brady just very politely and professionally buried Aaron Rodgers,” Bailey wrote. Not everyone thought Brady went quite that far. One fan called it “a light scolding for Aaron Rodgers from Tom Brady there.” Some fans also praised the way Brady handled such a touchy subject on live TV. “Brady, in a very professional way took care of the Rodgers situation. Well done,” one fan wrote. Taken together, the reaction showed how sharply Brady’s words cut, even in a mild tone. He praised Rodgers as a player and called a possible end to his career sad. But he also made clear that, in his view, airing a team’s private business in public crosses a line. As Brady pointed out, the Steelers now have to play on Friday while dealing with the fallout, and for many viewers his core message was easy to hear. (AP Photo/Scot Tucker) (Scot Tucker/AP) Vederian Lowe has picked Trent Williams ' brain and studied the generational left tackle's film since signing with the San Francisco 49ers in March, but the onetime sixth-round pick and part-time NFL starter understands there are limits to what he can replicate. "A lot of the things that he does, I can't do," Lowe said. "Because Trent is one of one." However, there is something Lowe has done that Williams has spent his illustrious 16-season career wishing he could do. On Nov. 17, 2024, Lowe, then with the Patriots, realized every 300-pound man's dream when he caught a 4-yard touchdown from quarterback Drake Maye in a loss to the Chargers. Asked where his lone catch ranks among his career highlights, Lowe smiled and invoked Williams, who is catch-less and has long lobbied head coach Kyle Shanahan for a goal-line pass. "That (catch) might be number one because they don't come by - I was talking to Trent and even Trent doesn't have one," Lowe said. "So I'm like, ‘OK.' That's up there for sure." The lofty ranking Lowe has assigned his reception speaks to the rarity of such a snag. But it also speaks to the modest number of highlights he's collected in a five-season career that has included 25 starts, just four since Jan. 5, 2025. But that could be changing. Last Sunday, in a 35-10 win over the Vikings in Mexico City, Lowe was unexpectedly thrust into the role of a key starter on a Super Bowl contender when right tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a broken and dislocated ankle in the second quarter . McKivitz's season is over. Lowe's chance to show why the 49ers signed him to a two-year contract with a maximum value of $12 million to serve as their swing tackle is just beginning. "That's why we brought him here," Shanahan said. "Anytime you have a swing tackle - that means you better be capable of starting. He's started a lot of games in this league and has played like a starter. And that's why we targeted him." Lowe is assuming some sizable cleats. McKivitz, 30, was earning every bit of the three-year, $45 million extension he signed last year by not allowing a sack in 327 pass-blocking snaps this season before his injury. The very early returns, however, are promising. On Lowe's first snap after replacing McKivitz, he pancaked defensive tackle Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins on a 10-yard run by Christian McCaffrey . It was the start of a 38-snap performance in which Lowe committed a false start, but he didn't allow a QB pressure on 19 pass-blocking snaps against Minnesota's chaotic, blitz-heavy defense, a unit which leads the NFL in sacks. Lowe did so despite logging most of his snaps at left tackle throughout his career. His only four starts at right tackle were in 2023 with the Patriots and he'd spent most of his practice time on the left side since joining the 49ers. "Swinging from both sides," Lowe said, "it's not an easy task at all." Center Jake Brendel wasn't surprised Lowe managed to make it look seamless. Brendel, 34, was struck by the questions Lowe was asking about the 49ers' intricate blocking schemes not long after his arrival. Lowe peppered Brendel with queries about "chokes," "blunts" and "seals," all backside blocks from tight ends or other players lined up outside the 49ers' offensive tackles. "He asked me questions that guys don't ask me until year three or four in the system," Brendel said. "So the guy knows football … A lot of backup tackles kind of just float around and then they go in and they're like, ‘All right, I'll get it done physically, but I'm not expecting to be at the level of a starter.' This guy's definitely starting (material)." The Patriots weren't convinced about Lowe's first-string ability. After Lowe made a season-high 13 starts in 2024, New England drafted left tackle Will Campbell with the No. 4 pick to replace him last year. Lowe made four starts as a fill-in in 2025 after making 21 starts the previous two seasons. After his step down in status, he joined the 49ers knowing he'd have no shot to unseat Williams or McKivitz. Now, however, he's a starter on a 9-1 team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. Lowe has a chance to help his new team earn a ring while showing he's more than a well-compensated backup. If last Sunday's performance was any indication, it's an opportunity he's ready to seize, much like that pass he caught in 2024, a moment even Williams can only hope to replicate. "The opportunity doesn't come by too often," Lowe said, "and I was not dropping that." Subscribe There’s more to San Francisco with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. title: Wu-Tang Clan takes over Detroit Lions’ Thanksgiving halftime show
summary: The legendary rap collective tore through decades of classics during the Lions-Bears game, with Eminem curating the performance and Chad
content: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 26: The Wu-Tang Clan performs the halftime show during the game between the Detroit Lions and the Chicago Bears at Ford Field on November 26, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Photo by: Gregory Shamus / Getty Images The legendary rap collective tore through decades of classics during the Lions-Bears game, with Eminem curating the performance and Chad Smith joining on drums. Thanksgiving came with a side of Shaolin at Ford Field. Wu-Tang Clan took over the Detroit Lions’ Thanksgiving Day halftime show on Thursday, delivering a rapid-fire run through the songs that helped establish the Staten Island collective as one of hip-hop’s most influential groups. The group hit the field during the Lions’ matchup against the Chicago Bears dressed in Detroit blue and backed by Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer Chad Smith. The group opened with “Triumph” before moving through a medley that reportedly included “Da Mystery of Chessboxin’,” “Protect Ya Neck,” “Method Man,” “Shimmy Shimmy Ya,” “Ice Cream,” “C.R.E.A.M.” and “Wu-Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit.” Young Dirty Bastard stepped in to represent his late father, founding Wu-Tang member Ol’ Dirty Bastard, during “Shimmy Shimmy Ya.” Before the show, he shared a backstage photo with Eminem, who helped bring the performance together. Eminem did not join Wu-Tang onstage, but his fingerprints were all over the production. According to Complex , the Detroit rapper and his longtime manager, Paul Rosenberg, served as executive producers and selected the group to headline the show. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Detroit Lions (@detroitlionsnfl) The performance marked the second year of their multiyear partnership with the Lions. In 2025, Eminem made a surprise appearance alongside Jack White during the team’s Thanksgiving game, performing “‘Till I Collapse” before the Detroit rock star closed the set with “Seven Nation Army.” When Wu-Tang’s appearance was announced earlier this month, Lions President and CEO Rich Haddad described the holiday game as one of sports’ greatest traditions and the group as one of music’s greatest acts. “We are thrilled to have Wu-Tang headlining our Thanksgiving halftime show and grateful to Marshall and Paul for their partnership,” Haddad said in the NFL’s announcement . The booking arrived during an already celebratory period for the group. Less than two weeks before the Thanksgiving performance, Wu-Tang Clan received the Early Influence Award at the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony. Chris Rock inducted the group, praising its members for building a global hip-hop force without relying on the traditional industry machine. Wu-Tang then performed another crowd-pleasing medley featuring “C.R.E.A.M.,” “Method Man” and “Shimmy Shimmy Ya.” The latest honor follows the group’s “Wu-Tang Forever: The Final Chamber” tour, which was announced as its final North American run. RZA previously described the tour as a chance for the members to come together once more and spread Wu-Tang’s music and culture around the world. Thursday’s halftime show proved that whether the stage is an arena, an awards ceremony or the middle of a football field, the Clan still knows how to command a crowd. title: ‘Zero Sense Outside Chicago Connection,’ ‘Dumbest Take’ — Fans Torch Colin Cowherd Over ‘Insane’ Caleb Williams-Michael Jordan Comparison
summary: Colin Cowherd posted about Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams on Thanksgiving, and fans quickly pushed back on his assessment of the young quarterback. content: Fans question Colin Cowherd's Caleb Williams-Michael Jordan comparison after the Bears quarterback rallies Chicago past the Detroit Lions. Colin Cowherd posted about Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams on Thanksgiving, and fans quickly pushed back on his assessment of the young quarterback. The 39-35 victory over the Detroit Lions snapped Detroit’s six-game winning streak, gave Chicago its first NFC North win of the season, and left the Bears alone atop the division. Williams, the 2024 No. 1 overall pick, led the comeback with a touchdown in the final seconds. Fans Dismiss Colin Cowherd’s Michael Jordan Comparison for Caleb Williams Cowherd, host of “The Herd” on FS1, offered little explanation when he posted Thursday : “Caleb is a young MJ.” One fan responded , “This is an insane tweet (expletive).” Another wrote , “Please stop this.” Chicago trailed by 11 midway through the fourth quarter after Jahmyr Gibbs broke free for a 70-yard touchdown, his third score of the game. Williams answered with a 41-yard touchdown pass to Rome Odunze and ran in the two-point conversion to cut Detroit’s lead to 35-32. With three seconds left, he found Odunze again, this time for a 6-yard touchdown that put the Bears ahead for good. Cowherd had praised Williams before Thursday, including after the quarterback suffered a right hamstring injury in Week 2. On September 21, while his availability remained uncertain, Cowherd said : “When you’re as generationally gifted as Caleb, or LeBron, or Wemby, or Mahomes and Josh Allen, you’re not carrying a team, you’re carrying a league.” Not everyone agreed with his latest assessment. One fan remarked : “This makes zero sense outside of the Chicago connection.” Another added , “This is the dumbest take I’ve ever seen in my life. Just because they’re both in Chicago? Incredibly lazy comparison.” Williams completed 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards and 2 touchdowns against Detroit. Through Thanksgiving, he had 12 passing touchdowns and 6 interceptions in 8 appearances. A reply to Cowherd read: “10 TDs 7 INTs on the season. Basically a league average QB with high upside.” Another fan commented : “Michael Jordan was averaging 37.1 points a game in his 3rd year. Caleb Williams has 12 passing touchdowns in 11 games.” The Chicago Bulls legend’s 37.1-point average came during his third NBA season. Williams, meanwhile, had appeared in only 8 of Chicago’s 11 games at the time of the comparison. SEE ALSO: ‘Here We Go Again,’ ‘The Suffering Never Ends’ – Timberwolves Fans Brace for Worst After LaMelo Ball Goes Down With Ankle Injury vs. Thunder Williams’ development has given Chicago plenty to build on since his rookie season, when the Bears went 5-12. In 2025, he led the team to an 11-6 record, the NFC North title and its first playoff victory since 2010. He also set a Bears single-season passing record with 3,942 yards and earned the team’s 2025 Offensive Player of the Year honor. The quarterback helped produce seven wins in games Chicago trailed in the final two minutes that season, including six in the regular season and one in the playoffs. Thursday’s comeback added another late victory to his résumé, as the Bears improved to 9-2 and extended their winning streak to six games. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

title: Andy Reid disagrees with overturned Rashee Rice catch after Chiefs' loss to Bills: 'That was not clear and obvious'
summary: We may never know what a catch is in the NFL.
content: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice appeared to have a much-needed first down against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving. The NFL's replay center disagreed. With the game tied 10-10 and two minutes left in the fourth quarter, the Chiefs got the ball deep in their own territory. A pair of incompletions left them facing third-and-10, at which point Patrick Mahomes appeared to connect with wide receiver Rashee Rice for 11 yards and the first down. However, the play was surprisingly overturned on replay, with the official only saying, "After review, the ball hit the ground, it's an incomplete pass." This was ruled a catch for Rashee Rice on the field and was overturned to incomplete after review: pic.twitter.com/mh6QNXsnPJ — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 27, 2026 The call was popular at Buffalo's Highmark Stadium, but not so much on social media. The video replay indeed showed the ball hit the ground while pinned between Rice's right hand and shoulder, but that alone doesn't make the play an incomplete pass. The ball must also come loose while hitting the ground before Rice establishes possession, and that was very much up for debate. Additionally, the NFL maintains a "clear and obvious" standard for overturning plays. So the replay officials in New York City not only believed Rice hadn't completed the catch, they also decided it was clear to anyone watching. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid very much didn't seem to think that was the case after his team’s 13-10 defeat , via Kansas City's KSHB 41 : "Not [a call] that I agreed with, but yeah. This came from New York, so it's not from these guys. Our guys called it a completion, the guys who were working the game. I'm not quite sure what they saw. I saw he had control of the ball and his elbow hit and then the ball hit, but he had control. "Normally, in those kind of situations, it's gotta be clear and obvious. To me, that was not clear and obvious." Rashee Rice appeared to have a first down for the Chiefs. The NFL's replay center disagreed. AP Photo/Matt Rourke Mahomes' wife Brittany, meanwhile, used the occasion to dispute the idea the Chiefs have benefited from calls during their recent run, writing the following on her Instagram story : "HAHAHAHAHAHA WHAT A JOKE "Guess we can't even play football without getting it called against us… not sure what an actual catch is after that I guess? I don't wanna hear s*** anymore from anyone" She also posted a collection of social media posts criticizing the call to her story. NFL vice president of instant replay Mark Butterworth spoke to a pool reporter, pointing to Rice's hand moving up the ball as evidence that he lost control. The pool report with NFL VP of Instant Replay Mark Butterworth on the overturned ruling of a catch by Rashee Rice. “As the receiver is going to the ground, he had the ball in his right hand and when he contacted the ground, his hand slid up the ball and we deemed that a loss of… pic.twitter.com/Cl094uWVk0 — Matt Derrick (@mattderrick) November 27, 2026 To be clear, this play did not singlehandedly cost the Chiefs the game, though it's undeniably frustrating. Had the Rice catch stood, they still would have needed to travel half the field to reach field-goal range, on a day in which struggling kicker Harrison Butker made one field goal from 26 yards and missed another from 46. Facing fourth-and-10, Kansas City was instead forced to punt out of its own end zone. The teams immediately exchanged three-and-outs and appeared headed to overtime, only for field position to bite the Chiefs again when a disastrous punt sequence put the Bills in field-goal position for the final play.

content: Bob Frid-Imagn Images Gabe Perreault will miss four to six weeks due to a lower-body injury that has landed him on injured reserve. content: The Ottawa Senators are clearly open for business, as GM Steve Staios has been making the rounds, including a trip to Nashville to watch the Predators take on the Penguins. Now, there's a report that he could have inquired about a San Jose Sharks forward. On Wednesday, Senators columnist Bruce Garrioch shared the following : "A league executive told the Ottawa Citizen on Tuesday that the Senators have likely kicked the tires on 24-year-old winger Collin Graf of the San Jose Sharks." Now, it's important to note that there wasn't much detail beyond that. It doesn't sound like a legitimate trade offer has been made, at least not one that's been reported publicly. Graf's name entered the rumor mill last week when he was a healthy scratch for two consecutive games, but considering the fact that the Sharks signed him to a three-year contract extension in July, it doesn't seem likely that they'd be in a hurry to move on from the 24-year-old. At this stage, it simply seems like Staios inquired about Graf, as he likely has done with many players from many different teams. With that being said, the Senators and Sharks have been known to make trades, as both William Eklund and Fabian Zetterlund were sent to Canada's capital in recent years.

title: 2 Up, 2 Down: More Frustration As Sunderland Drop Europa League Points
summary: Sunderland and Jagiellonia played out a scrappy draw as our Europa League campaign misfired again. Our writers react.
content: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 26: Sunderland's Chris Rigg crosses the ball despite the attentions of Jagiellonia Bialystok's Jeremy Agbonifo during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 match between Sunderland AFC and Jagiellonia Bialystok at Stadium of Light on November 26, 2026 in Sunderland, United Kingdom. (Photo by Lee Parker - CameraSport via Getty Images) | CameraSport via Getty Images David Elliott says…. Well in, Timur! Tutierov deserves credit for his endeavour and willingness to fight for the cause. He also has that handy knack of being in the right place at the right time, which is invaluable for a front player. Robin Roefs stands out Roefs was excellent. I never bought in to the narrative that he has dropped off but rather he was left seriously exposed. He certainly saved our blushes. Shapeless Sunderland Our shape and press were not working. Somehow we’re allowing teams to play out from the back and then suddenly find acres of space to drive at our defence. The press is disjointed and confused; I can’t see the triggers that mean everyone pushes up and shuts down their options. A low-key atmosphere This one will be very unpopular, yet it saddens me to hear fans booing and singing the name of a player who has left us, and leaving the stadium early. The attendance was disappointing — I’m fully aware that AC Milan and Christmas are coming, but this is Europe and we don’t know when this will come round again. Jon Guy says… A decent point? It’s a stretch but we got another point. Arguably the easiest game of the eight and we made hard work of it, and I’m really polishing a turd here to say it was anything but disappointing. Thank God for Robin Roefs What player we have in our number one. If it wasn’t for him we’d be talking about a crushing defeat. Some great saves from our goalkeeper who has to be up there with the best in the league. Where’s the energy gone? It could be six down but the first is once again we simply don’t look like we have any energy and for a team with a coach who is meant to be a tactical genius, we didn’t look like we had a tangible game plan. It was a really poor effort and there was no intensity at all. Given this is a team which played last season with a really good press, this is a worry. As fans we want the players to put a shift in, but how many can say they came off the pitch physically spent? Another defensive nightmare The basic fundamental mistakes just keep on happening. What’s happened to the defence this season? We look so brittle at the back, and the players look so frightened. If the team has lost confidence in the back line, it’ll change the team’s whole approach. It’s becoming a major issue. Mark Ryan says… Robin Roefs keeps it respectable Great bit of shot stopping and hopefully he can bring this form into the Premier League as he was given far more efforts than anyone was expecting. General disappointment All the excitement, fanfare, buzz and league pain for the Europa League. It felt like the EFL Trophy as the standard of football was at best uninspiring , but in the main it was below that standard. Really, what’s the point? I wasn’t entertained and neither were the thousands that booed at the end. Soft-touch Sunderland? At times we were carved open like the turkeys we were. A reminder that Jagiellonia are ninth in Poland. They may have had most first-team players playing but various gifts from Reinildo et al, the result could and probably should’ve been worse. What have we done to Chris Rigg? Missing for most of the first half and only showed flashes of what he can produce. His movement was often non-existent; maybe one progressive pass and a shot. He wasn’t the worst performer but watching at times, he struggled to get into the game. Tom Albrighton says… I Know It’s Over The best part of that dirge was the referee putting us out of our misery five seconds early. The Sound of Silence A very quiet crowd was reflective of one of most abject Sunderland performances in years. An affront to anyone who endured the cold to watch a game with zero intensity and zero creativity. The silence at full time was particularly deafening. Automatic Stop I don’t know why we do it but once again we were subject to an evening where the default setting of the entire team was to put their foot on the ball, kill it and then go sideways and repeat ad infinitum. It hasn’t worked this season and it isn’t going to work this season, so stop doing it. We’d knock a crab sick with how much we go sideways. Over and Over The repetition of our slow play is becoming something of a bone of contention. Both wingers were absolutely hopeless but never helped by the fact the service they received was as equally as poor and their support was non-existent. I’d love to know what the coaches are seeing and thinking when it’s pretty clear to everyone that playing in such a way saps any and all creativity from them.

title: Juventus power past early wobble to put down Omonia Nicosia
summary: The Bianconeri pushed closer to a much-needed top eight finish.
content: TURIN, ITALY - NOVEMBER 26: Jeff Ekhator of Juventus celebrates with Francisco Conceicao after scoring an goal during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 match between Juventus and Omonia FC at Juventus Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Alberto Gandolfo - Juventus/Juventus FC via Getty Images) | Juventus FC via Getty Images Thanksgiving is always a weird time when it comes to watching football for us here in the States. Europe couldn’t give a flying (redacted) about American holidays, so I got two doses of my favorite football teams—one European and one American. And strangely, both of those games ended up following a somewhat similar pattern. My beloved Philadelphia Eagles came out completely flat in their Thanksgiving game against the Dallas Cowboys, but scraped back from a 21-3 deficit to pull out a last second win. (Duck Fallas) Juventus were similarly bad in the first half of their Europa League contest against Omonia Nicosia. Some shockingly awful defense on a corner kick saw the Cyprian side score on Italian soil for the very first time in their history, leaving the fans at the J Stadium again scratching their heads and readying the jeers. But Juve’s heavily rotated lineup began to work things out. Andrea Cambiaso scored a phenomenal long-range goal eight minutes ahead of the break, and Francisco Concieção’s neat assist to Jeff Ekhator saw the 20-year-old open his account for Juventus to put Juve ahead after the break. A pair of second half goals gave Juve a much more comfortable end than my Birds had, ending the game with a 4-1 victory that propelled them to second place in the League Phase table and kept them in line for a vital bye to the round of 16. Likely with an eye to Sunday’s huge game against Como, Luciano Spalletti rotated heavily and put out a somewhat experimental lineup that looked more like a 3-4-3 than anything else. Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram, Nico González, and Pierre Kalulu were all still missing due to injury. Norberto Neto started in goal for Juventus for the first time since 2017, anchoring a back three of Federico Gatti, Jhon Lucumí, and Lloyd Kelly. Cambiaso and Juan Cabal sandwiched the double pivot midfield of Pape Matar Sarr and Douglas Luiz, while Conceição and Jérémie Boga flanked Ekhator up top. Henning Berg countered with a 4-2-3-1. He was missing Fotis Kitsos and Mihlali Mayambela to injury, while four players—Carel Eiting, Moses Odubajo, David Akintola and Giorgos Viktoros—were cup-tied. Thomas Kaminski started in goal, guarded by Loïc Nego, Senou Coulibaly, Lubomír Satka, and Jean-Kévin Duverne. Mateo Maric and Panagiotis Andreou started in midfield, while Florin Tanase, Muamer Tankovic, and Jaden Montnor supported Andronikos Kakoullis in attack. Conceição worked himself into a shooting opening by paradoxically drifting backward, forcing Kaminski into an early save, but that was about as threatening as Juve looked in the early going. But they couldn’t come up with any more shots until the 15 minute mark, when Omonia lined up for a corner kick. Everything went wrong on this play. Satka and Kakoullis both ended up without a marker on the back post, and the former had an easy header after Neto flapped at the air as he tried to go for a punch, stunning the J Stadium into silence. Things were still off as play resumed. It toosk almost 10 minutes for Juve to muster their first semblance of a response in the form of a blocked Conceição shot, and seconds later Cabal let fly from distance and forced Kaminski to parry the ball back into the middle and hope no one in a black Juve shirt was there. But it was Omonia who were still providing more danger as the clock ticked into the latter stages of the half. That’s when Cambiaso turned back the clock a little bit. He took a simple pass from Conceição, cut inside a few steps, and let loose a rocket from 25 yards out that wouldn’t have been saved by anyone. That finally lit a fire under the squad, and Juve were on top six minutes later thanks to their new young striker. Andreou made a mistake in midfield and was robbed by Boga. Ekhator and Gatti swiftly pushed the ball to Conceição. Ekhator made a beautiful run between the center backs, Conceição hit him in stride, and the 20-year-old nutmegged Kaminski with a first-time shot to put Juve ahead. The Portuguese winger almost helped make it 3-1 before the break with a good run and lay-back to a marauding Gatti, but Kaminski made a good kick-save to deny him. Cambiaso nearly made it two wonder-strikes seconds into the second half, but Kaminski got a hand to it and Duverne got a block on the rebound by Conceição. Not long after, Boga drilled a ball just wide making clear that the two-goal outburst at the end of the half had put the momentum firmly into Juve’s lap. At one point Omonia had a 20-minute gap between shot attempts—and right after that Concieção put the game on ice. After receiving a pass from Weston McKennie he fired on target. Kaminski denied his first attempt with another kick-save, but the rebound came right back to the diminutive attacker, who made no mistake to put the ball into an open goal on his second try. Five minutes later Boga put things beyond all doubt, taking a pass from Cambiaso, giving a little bit of ground to open his shooting lane, then cracking the ball into the top corner. He hit it so hard Kaminski barely had time to move. Neto had to make one save in garbage time, but the Cyprian side wasn’t going to be pulling any miracles on this night, and Juve headed into the weekend with the momentum of an eight-goal week behind them as they get set for Sunday’s crunch match at Como.

title: 'Priceless' Duran proves 'the man' but is he papering over cracks at Celtic?
summary: Camilo Duran's 15-goal haul this season has made him an invaluable player for a Celtic side fighting for European progression.
content: "Duran is priceless for us at the moment". It would be difficult for a football manager to muster up a higher compliment for one of his players - given he should know exactly how much he did cost - but Celtic boss Martin O'Neill was rightly effusive in his praise for Camilo Duran. With 15 goals in 23 appearances, six assists, and another late European winner on Thursday, the Colombian was once again the main man for a struggling Celtic side. His double against Besiktas breathed life into their Europa League campaign last time out, and his late leap to nod in the winner against Torreense kept it alive. Duran, 24, started on the bench but was brought on with just over half an hour to go as O'Neill watched his side labour against a team currently 13th in the Portuguese second tier. Celtic would still be searching for their first European win were it not for their summer arrival from Qarabag, whose goals have played a key part in keeping his team within touching distance of a play-off spot with three fixtures to play. "He's taken on this mantle of being the man and he's been fantastic," said O'Neill, who started Duran on the bench. "We tried a similar approach against Besiktas. "Sometimes by the time Duran gets subbed on, you could be behind. But I think that's the sign of a brilliant player, he'll do something. "He's not a big guy but he's just a super footballer, a super, super footballer." Papering over cracks or quality in depth? Duran's summer arrival was overshadowed when, just over a fortnight later, a club-record fee was paid to Bodo Glimt for another striker, Kasper Hogh. While recent weeks have been dominated by debates over Duran or Hogh , the debate now seems settled, with the Colombian operating on a different level from his striking counterpart. Anyone watching Celtic in Portugal would have watched Hogh find space a handful of times in the area, but repeatedly fail to find a team-mate or trouble the goalkeeper. Duran didn't need to be asked twice. "I don't know how many touches he got, but he had the telling touch," James McFadden said on Sportsound post-match. Duran's goals have also proved decisive in securing domestic points against Falkirk and Hibernian, and with Celtic just a point clear of Rangers, he is indeed invaluable. Despite his late header giving the thousands of travelling Celtic fans a thrilling end to a relatively turgid game, the intervention is another significant moment in a season that is threatening to unravel if individual performances fail to continue papering over glaring deficiencies across the park. If the lively Jota - who lasted 74 minutes - was not creating chances, tormenting full-backs or digging out enticing crosses in the first half, Celtic seemed without any real plan of attack. Yang and Luke McCowan's involvements were limited at best, Hogh's chance to stake a claim was sub-par to be kind, and there was no driving force from the middle of the park to show some impetus. Arithmetically, Celtic can still finish in any position in the Europa League table. But if they are to claim a playoff or automatic qualification spot, they will need Duran to remain in such a rich vein of form. Duran spares Celtic's blushes against Portuguese second-tier side Torreense Celtic news, views and analysis all in one place What are the fans saying? Brian: Embarrassed by that performance, I know that there no easy games in Europe, couldn't pass the ball, not fit enough, no style of play and poorly coached. The club is in decline. John: Celtic are just an average side these days - there should be no expectation. Ted: That was just embarrassing. The 31st team in Portugal made us look ordinary. Go now Martin with dignity intact and preserve your achievements. Thus mob will drag you down. Allan: Outclassed and out paced by Torreense, Celtic played poorly with a lot of comedy of errors in their play. But Yippee hee, Celtic. Won with a late goal from Duran. Liam: This can't go on any further now, regardless of the result. MON is done and the coaching staff are done. Booing substitutions is the end, never mind a performance like this against second division opposition. The board can resign too. Alec: Total embarrassment. Barring Jota, there was a complete lack of creativity, quality, urgency and belief. Time for the board to make the right decisions, get a new manager in and get rid of at least 10 of those players on show tonight.

title: Rangers Boss in Favour of Keeping Findlay Curtis at Club
summary: Derek McInnes prepares to rebuff loan offers for Scotland’s youngest World Cup star as contract negotiations loom, prioritising the dynamic winger's long-term future at Rangers this winter.
content: According to a report by media outlet Football Insider , via TransferFeed , Scottish Premiership side Rangers manager Derek McInnes is not in favour of sending out 20-year-old Scottish winger Findlay Curtis on loan during the upcoming transfer window. The boss of the Glasgow club is reportedly in favour of retaining the player. In addition to this news by Football Insider, there was also a previous one reported by TransferFeed which said that talks of a contract extension were underway between Rangers and Curtis. However, the news in question also mentioned that even after negotiating for several months, a definitive conclusion could not be reached by the parties involved. The report stated, “Curtis stated that he will leave the matter with his agent and the football club.” Born in 2006, Curtis joined the academy of Rangers in 2012, at the age of 6, and came up through the hierarchy of the club to make his first-team debut in 2025. Ten days after making his debut, he signed a contract extension with Rangers, the length of which has remained undisclosed. Since then, the player has made 22 official league appearances for the Gers and has netted 1 goal, an equaliser scored against St Mirren. He has also played 2 Scottish Cup, 4 League Cup, and 9 European games for Rangers. In 2026, Curtis joined fellow Premiership side Kilmarnock on a loan deal, where he further featured in 14 league games and scored 5 goals. In addition to his club career, the 20-year-old has also made 6 official appearances for the senior squad of the Scotland National Football Team, after playing a mere 2 games for the U-21 squad of The Tartan Army. He became Scotland’s youngest ever player to feature on the field in a World Cup when he came on as a second-half substitute during Scotland's game against Haiti at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, overtaking the record of teammate Ben Gannon-Doak. As things stand, it does not look like Findlay Curtis would be going out on loan during the upcoming January transfer window. However, if the club indeed wants to retain the player, it will have to provide him with regular playing time. A contract extension is also necessary to bind the player to the club, and a definitive conclusion to the negotiations would have to be reached quickly before other clubs show their interest and the youngster decides to leave.

title: Southend United legend awarded Freedom of the City
summary: Frankie Banks admits feeling emotional as he accepts the prestigious civic honour.
content: Frankie Banks has been involved with the Shrimpers for almost 60 years [Warren Muggleton/BBC] A legendary ex-Southend United footballer has been awarded the Freedom of the City for his lifelong service to the Shrimpers. Frankie Banks was granted the prestigious civic honour at a meeting of Southend-on-Sea City Council on Thursday evening. The 81-year-old's love affair with Roots Hall began in 1958 and has continued for almost 60 years, in the form of playing, coaching and community outreach roles. He was visibly moved as Blues supporters gave him a standing ovation from the council chamber's public gallery. "It was emotional and that's me, I'm afraid. This football club is a very important part of my life," Banks told the BBC. He was first spotted by Southend while playing football in a park near Roots Hall in 1958, and went on to make 79 appearances for the first team across two stints. Banks enjoyed two spells at Roots Hall, before spending time in the dugout [Tom Larsen-Wright/BBC] Banks signed for Hull City in 1966 but returned to the Essex coast in 1976, playing for three more years before his retirement. The steely right-back, who was born in Hull but grew up in Southend, then transitioned into a youth coach and rose to become the club's assistant manager. "The club means so much to me. They gave me the opportunity to become a professional footballer," he said. "The reason I love this club [is] the supporters… They're fantastic, really fantastic people." Banks became Southend United's first football in the community officer in 1991 and, despite retiring in 2007, has continued to serve the foundation. He still coaches multiple teams, including the Shrimpers' walking football team, and volunteers at after-school clubs. Daniel Cowan, the council's Labour leader, nominated Banks for the award and said it was "high time we made a little more noise about our unsung hero". Conservative councillor James Courtenay, who backed the motion, added: "Generations of Southenders have been touched by his work." Do you have a story suggestion for Essex? Contact us below. title: Sunderland Have The Tools To Make Themselves Safe
summary: With their best eleven Sunderland have enough to climb the table, but they must get their recruitment right in January.
content: Two clean sheets and four points from two of the better teams in the Premier League has been a welcome reversal in what had been a slump that took us to the bottom of the table. To put it bluntly and trying not to talk like David Moyes, but if anyone had been in any doubt before our trip to Coventry a couple of weeks ago, we are at this point in a relegation battle. The points tally doesn’t lie, the goals conceded tally doesn’t lie, nor the goal difference. If anyone wants to argue that we are too good to be in one, then that is the kind of complacency which sees such supposedly ‘ too good to go down ‘ suffer the dreaded drop. However, if anything the win at home against Chelsea and the point gained from the trip to Aston Villa have shown that we do have the tools to get out of trouble. Against Chelsea we looked the better team. Villa were restricted at arms length until the last ten minutes of the game. These two performances were more like the Sunderland of last season which fought for every point. The problem this Sunderland squad has, and which has played a part in the slump that took us to the bottom of the table is that they badly miss key players when they are injured. Glaringly obvious in the case of Brian Brobbey, but just as importantly in the case of Nordi Mukiele. With his return, the defensive mistakes which had been handing goals on a plate to our opponents in the previous games came to a halt and his knack of making the vital interceptions and clearances made all the difference at the back in the last two matches. Similarly with Brian Brobbey, Sunderland are a different team with him in the team not just because of the constant threat he brings, but also the ball is held up when it is played forward to him and an attack built around him. When he isn’t in the side we struggle to find that outlet. For all the repeated criticism of our summer recruitment of players we brought in, you have to cast an eye on two players who we didn’t keep hold of for different reasons this summer – Lutsharel Geertruida and Eilezer Mayenda. Geertruida would surely have been a starter in our back four with the likes of Ballard and Mukiele out and others out of form. If we were looking for a ball player who could play in the back four, why didn’t we sign up the one who had proven he could do the job? Mayenda didn’t get much game time last season, but in my opinion – and this is just the opinion of this fan – Wilson Isidor is a player who has to be playing at his maximum to be an effective starter in the Premier League. He was used to great effect as an impact sub last season, and scored quite a few important goals, but I always felt Mayenda had the greater potential, not least because he had the ability to play a perfectly timed through ball which was simply priceless. One position where we have found a very able deputy for an injured player is in Granit Xhaka’s anchor role in midfield where Jules Ahoka has added to his growing catalogue of impressive performances. All fingers crossed that we have no more injuries to key positions in the coming weeks, that Brobbey returns soon along hopefully with Dan Ballard. Two games a week is the reality this season, and injuries are part of that reality. Regis Le Bris has actively tried to rotate his team, but factor in a World Cup hangover where we had 13 players present and an AFCON in January which no Premier League club sent more players to than Sunderland, then some of our squad have been playing football non stop since June 2025 with two major tournaments thrown in. Little wonder there have been injuries and loss of form among so many. Our January shopping list surely must be for a centre back and striker to confidently cover the key areas, because we have shown that with a strong eleven on the pitch we can compete and take points off the better teams in the Premier League, what we need is quality cover for the key areas when our best players are injured.

title: Andrey Rublev shares his honest opinion about Mirra Andreeva as both a tennis player and person
summary: Andrey Rublev experienced playing alongside Mirra Andreeva at the US Open this year. Andreeva has won Roland Garros and the WTA Finals this year, in...
content: Andrey Rublev experienced playing alongside Mirra Andreeva at the US Open this year. Andreeva has won Roland Garros and the WTA Finals this year, in what has been a big breakthrough season for the Russian teenager, who has a big opportunity to become world number one at the start of the 2027 season. Although they had played an exhibition set together before, the US Open mixed doubles was the first time Andreeva and Rublev had played together in a professional setting. Andreeva and Rublev made it all the way to the semi-finals, beating two-time defending champions Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori en route, before they were beaten by eventual champions Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik . Three months on from playing with Andreeva, Rublev has revealed what he really thinks about his compatriot. Andrey Rublev backs Mirra Andreeva to achieve a lot more in her career While Andreeva has mostly had success this year, it has been a mixed season for former world number five Rublev, who dropped outside the top 20 for the first time in six years this season. Following the conclusion of his 2026 season, Rublev appeared on the The Blueprint , where he was asked about Andreeva and his experience of playing with her at the US Open this year. Rublev was full of praise for Andreeva, who he predicted would go on to achieve a lot more success in her career. “She’s such a good, joyful, bright, sunny child, incredibly talented, who has already achieved a lot and will achieve even more,” said Rublev. “I knew right away it would be a great atmosphere [US Open mixed doubles], so yeah, I think we had a blast. We also managed to show a good level of play, considering neither Mirra nor I are doubles players. It left behind some great memories that I’ll definitely cherish.” Andreeva has played with both Rublev and Daniil Medvedev , the latter of whom she lost in the first round with, in US Open mixed doubles since the event was overhauled in 2025. It will be interesting to see if Andreeva partakes in the event again in 2027 and if she reunites with either Rublev or Medvedev, or if she has a new partner.
